title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Multi-cycle M-unit (iterative divider + registered multiplier) and redirect cut from the fetch NOP mux
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz: the worst path is 199.8 ns / 150 logic levels,
forward mux -> alu.sv -> EX/MEM.alu_result (absorbed into the dmem BSRAM
address register). alu.sv implements DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU as combinational
32-bit `/` and `%` inside the forwarded single-cycle EX path, so every
instruction pays for an array divider CoreMark almost never uses.
iter/cycle is already 2.2 CoreMark/MHz; the whole deficit is Fmax.

Measured with Gowin (place option 0) on throw-away RTL copies during
hypothesis generation (timing only, not functional):
  - divider arms stubbed out, multiplier still combinational:
      46.5 MHz, 2110 LUT (baseline 5.44 MHz, 12312 LUT). New worst path:
      regfile BSRAM -> EX fwd mux -> branch compare -> redirect ->
      if_stage NOP mux -> hazard_unit -> ID/EX (26.8 ns).
  - same + `redirect` removed from if_stage's instr NOP mux:
      51.8 MHz, 13 levels. Worst path is then regfile BSRAM -> EX ->
      combinational DSP multiplier -> dmem BSRAM address (24.6 ns).
  - divider and multiplier both stubbed: 49.95 MHz before the redirect cut.
So three things stack on the same EX cone, in this order: divider,
redirect->fetch-NOP path, multiplier.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the M-extension a multi-cycle unit that stalls in EX, and remove a
logically redundant term that puts branch resolution in front of decode.

1. Divider: radix-2 restoring FSM, 1 quotient bit per cycle (~34 cycles
   incl. operand capture and sign fix-up). Operands (abs values + sign
   flags) are captured into registers on the start cycle; per-cycle logic
   is one 33-bit subtract + mux. RV32M corners: suppress quotient negation
   when divisor == 0 (-> all ones, remainder = dividend); INT_MIN / -1
   falls out of the unsigned datapath (q = 0x80000000, r = 0).
2. Multiplier: 2 cycles. Cycle 0 registers the forwarded operands as
   33-bit values sign/zero-extended per MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU, so ONE
   33x33 signed product replaces the three 64-bit products (6 DSP -> 2).
   Cycle 1 selects low/high half from those registers into EX/MEM. If the
   DSP -> EX/MEM path is still the worst path in `make timing`, also
   register the product (3-cycle MUL).
3. `ex_busy` = M op in ID/EX whose result is not ready. hazard_unit:
   ex_busy holds PC and ID/EX (stall, no flush) and EX/MEM captures a
   bubble (valid=0, ctrl='0). dmem_stall keeps priority (EX/MEM holds).
   The M-unit keeps running during dmem_stall, parks in a done state and
   returns to idle only on the cycle EX/MEM really accepts the result
   (!stall_ex_mem) - the same condition that lets ID/EX advance. M ops
   never redirect and never set mem_read, so flush_id/load-use do not
   interact with ex_busy.
4. Forwarding sources drain while EX is busy (EX/MEM gets bubbles, MEM/WB
   moves on). The M-unit latches its operands on the start cycle, and on
   every cycle ID/EX is held the forwarded rs1/rs2 are written back into
   ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val (operand refresh) so the EX operand muxes - and
   the RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata captured into EX/MEM at completion - stay
   correct after the producers have retired.
5. Formal: wrapper_si.sv BMC depth is 20 and a PREUNSAT on channel 0 is a
   failure, so under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS keep the identical
   start/busy/done handshake but return the ALTOPS formulas with a short
   fixed latency (2 cycles for MUL and for DIV), so every M insn check and
   liveness can still reach a retirement inside the window.
6. if_stage: `out.instr = (flush || redirect) ? NOP : imem_data` ->
   NOP only on imem stall. This is logically a no-op: whenever redirect=1
   the ID/EX register is either flushed (flush_id) or held (dmem_stall),
   so it never captures the IF payload, and the instruction in EX is a
   branch/jump (mem_read=0) so load_use_hazard is 0 whatever instr shows.
   PC update and flush_id keep using redirect unchanged. It removes the
   branch-compare -> redirect -> instr -> hazard/regfile-address path
   (46.5 -> 51.8 MHz measured).

Expected Fmax 52-65 MHz versus 5.44 MHz. Cycle cost: +1 cycle per MUL
(a few percent of CoreMark instructions) and ~33 cycles per DIV/REM
(rare): roughly 2-4% more cycles. Net fitness should rise about 9-11x
(12.1 -> ~105-130 iter/s); the stated delta is capped at +50 by the
schema range. Area drops from 12.3k to about 2.3k LUT4.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-001-r1s0 (improvement, +976.40%): Baseline Fmax (5.44 MHz, 150 logic levels) was set entirely by the combinational `/` and `%` in alu.sv sitting inside the forwarded single-cycle EX cone, so moving RV32M into a stalling multi-cycle unit (muldiv.sv: 34-cycle radix-2 restoring divider, 2-cycle MUL from registered 33-bit operands sharing one 33x33 product; `ex_busy` holds PC + ID/EX and bubbles EX/MEM) took fitness 12.1 -> 130.5 iter/s because CoreMark almost never divides and the extra MUL/DIV cycles cost only a few percent — keep rare deep ops out of the every-instruction path, and when stalling in EX remember that forwarding sources drain (refresh ID/EX rs1/rs2 values while held), that RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS needs a short fixed latency to retire inside the 20-step BMC, and that `redirect` in if_stage's instr NOP mux is redundant with flush_id yet puts branch-compare in front of hazard_unit/decode (the next critical path once the divider is gone, ~46.5 -> 51.8 MHz in stub runs), leaving regfile BSRAM -> fwd mux -> DSP multiply / branch compare as the remaining EX limit.

title: Multi-cycle M-unit: iterative divider + registered DSP multiplier with an EX-stall handshake
motivation:
The baseline's Fmax is 5.44 MHz because the worst path (199.8 ns, 156 logic
cells: MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> ex_stage -> alu -> EX/MEM / dmem address)
runs through the single-cycle combinational `/` and `%` in alu.sv, with the
three combinational 32x32->64 `*` products right behind it. Every instruction
pays a 200 ns clock for an operation CoreMark almost never executes (DIV/REM)
and one it executes a few percent of the time (MUL). A plain 5-stage pipeline
without those two operators in the EX cone closes at tens of MHz on the
GW2AR-18, so this single path costs roughly an order of magnitude of fitness.
The combinational dividers are also most of the 12.3k LUT4 (target 10k).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take MUL*/DIV*/REM* out of the single-cycle ALU and execute them in a new
multi-cycle unit (rtl/muldiv.sv) that holds the instruction in EX until the
result is ready. The ALU keeps only the 11 RV32I ops.

Unit (one small FSM: IDLE -> BUSY(count) -> DONE, shared by all ops):
  * Start cycle (M-op valid in ID/EX, FSM idle): latch the post-forward
    rs1/rs2 and the op. Latching is mandatory, not an optimisation: while the
    M-op waits in EX the older instructions drain through MEM/WB, so the
    EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding sources disappear and ID/EX.rs?_val may be
    stale. The forwarded values are correct in the start cycle even when it
    coincides with a dmem stall (EX/MEM and MEM/WB data are held then).
    EX/MEM.rs1_val / rs2_val / write_data (RVFI rs1_rdata / rs2_rdata) must
    come from these latched copies when the M-op finally leaves EX.
  * Multiply: ONE 33x33 signed multiplier (operands sign- or zero-extended
    to 33 bits per op: MUL/MULHU uu, MULH ss, MULHSU su) replacing the three
    64-bit products. It is fed from the latched operand registers (these map
    onto the DSP input registers); in the next cycle the low/high half is
    selected and written to EX/MEM: 2 cycles in EX = 1 stall cycle per MUL.
    A localparam adds a product register (3 cycles in EX) to be enabled only
    if `make timing` shows the DSP on the worst path.
  * Divide: radix-2 restoring divider on magnitudes, 1 bit per cycle (one
    33-bit subtract + mux per step, ~35 cycles in EX) with sign fix-up of
    quotient/remainder. RV32M corner cases: divide-by-zero must give
    q = 0xFFFFFFFF (suppress the quotient negation when b == 0) and
    r = dividend; INT_MIN / -1 gives q = INT_MIN, r = 0 (falls out of the
    magnitude datapath).
  * Under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the unit returns the XOR-of-add/sub
    stand-ins alu.sv uses today, computed from the latched operands through
    the SAME FSM with the counter preloaded for a fixed 2-cycle latency for
    every op. formal/checks_si.cfg has `liveness 1 10 20` and BMC depth 20
    with both ready inputs tied to 1, so a 35-cycle wait would fail the
    per-iteration gate; the short ALTOPS latency keeps it inside budget while
    the stall/bubble/latched-operand path itself is still proven. Real
    arithmetic stays covered by cocotb vectors and cosim (as today).
    Yosys-frontend-safe SV only (no `function ... return`, no packages).

Pipeline handshake (m_wait = M-op valid in EX && FSM not DONE; depends only
on ID/EX control bits and FSM state flops, never on datapath values):
  * hazard_unit: stall_if and stall_id also assert on m_wait (PC and ID/EX
    hold); flush_id is untouched (an M-op is never a load, branch or jump,
    so load-use and redirect cannot originate from it).
  * EX/MEM register priority: dmem_stall -> hold (unchanged); else m_wait ->
    capture a bubble ('0), so the instruction in MEM moves on and retires
    exactly once and a store in EX/MEM is never presented for a second
    ready cycle (the bus model commits a write on every wen && ready cycle);
    else capture (M result when the instruction is an M-op).
  * The FSM keeps DONE and its result stable until EX/MEM really takes it
    (DONE && !dmem_stall), then returns to IDLE in the same edge that ID/EX
    advances, so a dmem stall on the completion cycle neither drops nor
    repeats the op and back-to-back M-ops restart cleanly.
  * The M result is merged after the ALU's own result mux
    (m_op ? m_result : alu_result) so it does not deepen the RV32I path.

Expected effect: the EX cone shrinks to forward mux -> 32-bit adder /
shifter / comparator -> result mux, which should close at roughly 40-60 MHz
instead of 5.4 MHz (7-10x). IPC cost: one stall cycle per MUL (a few percent
of CoreMark's instructions, nearly all in the matrix kernels) and ~34 per
DIV/REM (rare in the timed region) - about 3% more cycles than the baseline's
449k cycles/iteration. Net fitness gain is several hundred percent, far above
the +50 this field can express, and well clear of the 4.6% acceptance
noise band. Area falls by thousands of LUT4 and the DSP count drops from 6.
Known limitation: `make formal-deep` (no ALTOPS, not in the loop) would need
a larger liveness bound for the real 35-cycle divide; the per-iteration gate
is unaffected.

changes.description: New module: start/busy/done multi-cycle M-extension unit. Latches post-forward operands and op on start; single 33x33 signed multiplier fed from the operand registers (optional product register via localparam); radix-2 restoring divider with sign fix-up and RV32M div-by-zero / overflow results; ALTOPS branch returning the riscv-formal stand-in formulas through the same FSM with a fixed 2-cycle latency. Wire m_wait from ex_stage to hazard_unit. Top-level IO and the RVFI port set are unchanged.

Keep the RV32I vectors on alu.sv; move the M-extension vectors out (alu.sv no longer implements them).

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-002-r1s1 (regression, +731.27%): The same stalling multi-cycle M-unit as the merged r1s0 (here latching post-forward operands inside muldiv.sv rather than refreshing ID/EX; both variants passed formal + cosim) but with no other timing change scored 100.75 vs r1s0's 130.46 iter/s — +731% over the old 12.12 baseline yet a lost round — because the implied Fmax is only ~46 MHz (inferred from fitness at ~459k cycles/iter; this slot's timing report was not available to the scribe), which matches r1s0's 46.5 MHz divider-stub measurement where regfile BSRAM -> fwd mux -> branch compare -> `redirect` -> if_stage instr NOP mux -> hazard_unit -> ID/EX takes over as the worst path: removing one dominant path only buys Fmax up to the next one, so stub out the offender and run timing during hypothesis generation to find and fix the follow-on path in the same change (the `redirect` cut was worth roughly +29% fitness on top of the M-unit), and do not re-propose the M-unit itself — it is already in the champion.

title: Fetch-cycle pre-decoded branch prediction: 2-bit bimodal PHT direction + in-IF pc+imm target (no BTB)
motivation:
The core has no branch prediction: every taken conditional branch and every
JAL/JALR is resolved in EX and kills the instruction fetched behind it
(flush on `redirect`), costing one fetch slot per taken control-flow
instruction. Baseline CoreMark under the scored 22% iStall/dStall bench is
4,491,485 cycles for 10 iterations (~2.93M instructions, CPI 1.53), and a
large slice of that is redirect bubbles. Fmax is set by a ~200 ns
forward->ALU (combinational divider) path, so logic added in the fetch
stage and on the EX redirect compare is nowhere near critical: the IPC gain
converts 1:1 into fitness.

Measured, not estimated: I prototyped this in a scratch copy of the RTL and
ran the exact fitness sim (cosim_sim coremark.elf --bench --istall --dstall,
all CRCs + "Correct operation validated" OK):
  baseline                         4,491,485 cycles
  bimodal 256x2b  (this proposal)  4,193,175 cycles  => +7.11% iter/cycle
  gshare 256x2b, 8-bit history     4,206,876 cycles  => +6.77%
  gshare 1024x2b, 10-bit history   4,188,141 cycles  => +7.24%
Global history buys nothing here, so the simplest table (bimodal) is chosen.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Because imem is read combinationally (IF/ID is a wire; the instruction is
visible in the same cycle as its PC), no BTB is needed: the fetch stage
pre-decodes the instruction and computes the exact target itself.

1. IF pre-decode (if_stage): is_jal_f = imem_data[6:0]==7'b1101111,
   is_br_f = imem_data[6:0]==7'b1100011; imm_f = is_jal_f ? J-imm : B-imm;
   bj_target = pc + imm_f (dedicated adder).
2. Direction: JAL always taken. Conditional branches read a 256-entry table
   of 2-bit saturating counters, `logic [1:0] pht [0:255]`, async read at
   pht_idx = pc[9:2], sync write, `initial` all entries 2'b01 (no reset, so
   it can map to distributed RAM); taken when pht_ctr[1].
3. pred_taken = !(flush || redirect) && (is_jal_f || (is_br_f && pht_ctr[1]))
                && bj_target[1:0]==2'b00.
   (flush_if already includes the imem stall, so this means "instruction
   really delivered"; misaligned targets are never predicted and keep the
   existing EX trap path with the PC staying linear.)
   next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target : pred_taken ? bj_target : pc + 4;
   the PC register keeps its existing priority (reset > redirect > !stall),
   so load-use / dmem / imem stalls simply re-predict the held instruction.
4. if_id_t and id_ex_t gain pred_taken, pht_idx[7:0], pht_ctr[1:0]; id_stage
   latches them (flush clears them with the rest of the payload).
5. EX verifies (ex_stage):
     actual_redirect = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault;
     redirect        = (actual_redirect != in.pred_taken);
     redirect_target = !actual_redirect ? in.pc + 4
                     : is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target;
   A correctly predicted taken branch / JAL raises no redirect (0 bubbles,
   today 1); JALR is never predicted and behaves as today; a branch wrongly
   predicted taken (incl. illegal funct3 2/3 encodings) is repaired to
   pc + 4. pc_next / RVFI pc_wdata stay computed from the architectural
   outcome exactly as now. hazard_unit is unchanged: redirect still means

title: Shorten the EX cone: LUT-RAM regfile, ID-registered forwarding selects, single WB data reg, late-adder ALU mux
motivation:
Champion Fmax is 58.9-59.8 MHz; iter/cycle is fine, Fmax is the deficit.
`make timing` on the champion: all five worst paths (22.29 ns arrival,
16.96 ns data) start at the regfile BSRAM and cross the whole EX cone:
  BSRAM clk-to-out 2.26 ns -> write-first bypass LUT in ID (1.3 ns)
  -> EX forwarding mux, 3 LUT levels behind the forward_unit compares
     (3.1 ns) -> alu_a mux (1.1 ns) -> adder (2.2 ns)
  -> SIX LUT levels of result mux after the adder (ALU op case +
     is_jump pc+4 + m_result, 5.1 ns) -> EX/MEM hold mux -> dmem BSRAM
     address (2.0 ns).
Path 4/5 are the same front end -> branch compare -> redirect -> flush_id
-> ID/EX reset. So ~6.7 ns is spent before the ALU sees an operand and
~5 ns after the adder is done. None of that is architectural.

Measured during hypothesis generation with Gowin (place option 0) on a
throw-away copy with the four edits below (timing only, NOT functionally
validated): 58.85 -> 80.35 MHz (+36.5%), 13 logic levels, 2421 LUT,
480 FF, 32 LUT-RAM, BSRAM 6 -> 4, DSP 2. New worst paths (17.74 ns
arrival): EX/MEM.alu_result -> fwd mux -> ALU -> dmem address, and
MEM/WB.alu_result -> EX -> branch compare -> redirect -> ID/EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Cycle-exact micro-optimisation of the EX path (no pipeline change, same
cycle count, so iter/cycle stays at the champion's 4,585,414 cycles):

1. Regfile as distributed LUT-RAM with asynchronous read in ID. Drop the
   32-entry reset loop (x0 is already forced to 0 on read; add an
   `initial` zero-fill for simulation, guard it if it blocks inference)
   and mark the array `/* synthesis syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" */`.
   Gowin currently folds the regfile + ID/EX rs?_val into a BSRAM, so EX
   starts with a 2.26 ns BSRAM clk-to-out plus the bypass LUT; with
   LUT-RAM the read + write-first bypass happen in ID (fed by the fetch
   word) and ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val are plain flops.

2. Forwarding selects computed in ID and registered with ID/EX (same
   enable as ID/EX, i.e. !stall_id): for the instruction in ID compare
   its rs1/rs2 against the rd of the instruction in ID/EX (-> select
   "EX/MEM" next cycle) and against the rd of the instruction in EX/MEM
   (-> select "MEM/WB" next cycle), priority EX/MEM > MEM/WB, rd != x0.
   This is equivalent to today's EX-time compare because ID/EX only
   captures when !stall_id, and then both older stages advance by exactly
   one. Hold cases: dmem_stall freezes ID/EX, EX/MEM and the MEM/WB data
   fields together, so the registered selects stay right; under ex_busy
   the sources drain but muldiv samples its operands on the start cycle
   only and the ALU/branch results of an M op are unused (RVFI rs?_rdata
   already comes from m_rs?_q). The writer enables must be the post-trap
   ones: EX's ctrl_with_trap.reg_write for the ID/EX instruction
   (misaligned JAL/JALR does not write) and MEM's ctrl_with_trap.reg_write
   for the EX/MEM instruction (misaligned load does not write).

3. One WB data register: MEM/WB.alu_result captures
   `mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result` (mux moved in front of the
   register), wb_w_data = that register. The MEM/WB forwarding source and
   the regfile write data become a flop output instead of a mux.

4. Late-arriving adder selected last: alu.sv exposes the add/sub result
   separately; EX/MEM.alu_result <= sel_add ? add_out : (is_jump ? pc+4 :
   m_op ? m_result : other_alu_out) with sel_add derived from ID/EX flops
   (ideally a pre-decoded bit in ctrl_t), so only one mux level follows
   the carry chain instead of six.

If timing shows headroom to chase after these (the implementer should run
`make timing`, ~1 min): one-hot registered selects for a flatter fwd mux,
and a flatter redirect (single eq/lt compare selected by pre-decoded
bits; pc[1:0] is always 0 so branch/JAL misalign is just imm[1]).

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-001-r2s0 (improvement, +63.97%): The whole gain is Fmax (59.8 -> 98.1 MHz, median of 96.8/98.1/98.1 over place options; CoreMark cycles unchanged at 4,585,414, +18 LUT4, formal 53/53 first try) and came from removing everything that is not data-dependent from the single-cycle EX cone over three `make timing` -> fix -> re-validate passes inside one slot: (1) the four planned edits reached 79.2 MHz, as the hypothesis-time prototype predicted (80.35) — a regfile with a reset loop is folded by Gowin into a BSRAM together with ID/EX.rs?_val (2.26 ns clk-to-out + bypass LUT at the head of EX), whereas no reset loop + `initial` zero-fill + `syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"` + `!reset`-gated write infers 32 LUT-RAM cells with read/bypass in ID (BSRAM 6 -> 4), the forwarding selects are compared in ID against ID/EX.rd and EX/MEM.rd with the post-trap `reg_write` bits and registered with ID/EX, the load/ALU mux moves in front of MEM/WB, and a pre-decoded `sel_add` picks the adder in the last mux level; (2) 87.2 MHz from pre-muxing op_a/op_b in ID (own `fwd_a`/`fwd_b`, forced 00 for pc/imm), a one-hot AND-OR ALU with one shared SRL/SRA shifter, and a dedicated `EX/MEM.mem_addr <= rs1 + imm` (the JALR adder) driving `io_dmemAddr`, because Gowin absorbs the address flop into the dmem BSRAM so the entire EX result mux otherwise sits in front of the BSRAM address pins; (3) 97-100 MHz from deciding branch/JAL target alignment in ID (`br_ok/br_bad/jal_ok/jal_bad`) and using one `==` plus one unsigned `<` (sign fix-up and invert folded into `cmp_flip`) so only ~2 LUT levels follow the compare chain into `redirect` — so compute in ID and register anything EX needs that depends only on instruction bits or register numbers, check which flops Gowin has folded into a BSRAM at either end of a worst path, and keep looping on the timing report within the slot (the two follow-on passes were worth +24% beyond the planned edits); things later iterations must respect: the registered selects are correct only while ID/EX captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB each advance by one instruction (ex_busy is safe only because muldiv latches its operands on the start cycle), so any new stall, bubble, flush or stage must re-establish that; clearing only the control bits of ID/EX on `flush_id` passed formal but measured 88.4 vs 99.7 MHz on option 0 (cause not diagnosed, do not retry blind); place options spread about +/-1.5 MHz, so `make timing` (option 0 only) cannot rank changes under ~3% — use `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` for the scored median; and at 98 MHz two path families tie at ~15.6 ns arrival (~10.3 ns of data after 5.3 ns clock insertion) — forwarded MEM/WB value -> rs1/rs2 mux -> 32-bit compare chain -> `redirect` -> flush_id/PC, and `fwd_a` -> 3:1 mux -> adder/shifter -> EX/MEM.alu_result — so (scribe's inference, untested) more mux flattening is spent, further Fmax needs a structural cut of the forward -> compare -> `redirect` loop, and anything added to `redirect` (e.g. a predictor's mispredict XOR) now lands directly on a critical path.

title: Rebalance ID/EX: resolve operands in decode (LUT-RAM regfile + MEM/WB bypass in ID), EX keeps one registered-select 2:1 bypass
motivation:
The pipeline is badly unbalanced. In the timed bench the fetch+decode
stage is almost empty (imem data arrives from a register), while EX
carries everything. The champion's worst path (22.287 ns, 20 cells,
59.8 MHz) runs
  cpu/u_rf/regs (regfile, inferred by Gowin as a sync-read BSRAM that
  swallowed ID/EX.rs?_val) -> u_id (flush/write-first gating behind the
  BSRAM) -> u_ex 3:1 forward mux -> alu_src/auipc mux -> u_alu ->
  jump/M result mux -> dmem BSRAM address register (dmem_3).
So the EX cycle pays a BSRAM clock-to-out (several ns on GW2AR-18, vs
~0.4 ns for a flop), the bypass/flush gating Gowin adds behind that
BSRAM, a 3-input forward mux whose MEM/WB leg also contains the WB
mem_to_reg mux, and only then the ALU. forward_unit itself is NOT on
the reported path (its selects beat the BSRAM data), so merely
precomputing forward selects would not move Fmax. None of the operand
work before the ALU has to be in EX: for an instruction sitting in
decode, the results of the instructions in MEM and WB already exist in
that same cycle. Only the result of the instruction directly ahead
(in EX) is genuinely unavailable until the next cycle.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move operand resolution from EX into the decode stage so the EX cone
is flop -> one 2:1 bypass -> ALU, with identical cycle counts
(no new stall, no extra stage, same 1-cycle taken-branch and load-use
penalties; CoreMark stays at 4,585,414 cycles).

1. Regfile becomes an asynchronous-read distributed RAM (RAM16SDP4):
   drop the 32-entry reset loop, add `initial` zeroing for sim, tag
   the array syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram", keep the x0 read mux.
   ID/EX.rs1_val/rs2_val are then real flops, so EX launches from a
   flop clock-to-out instead of a BSRAM clock-to-out. Check in the
   Gowin log that BSRAM count drops 6 -> 4 (dmem only).
2. Decode-stage bypass network. For the instruction I in ID, per
   operand, priority:
     a. producer in MEM (EX/MEM.rd == rs, rd != 0, valid, post-trap
        reg_write, i.e. not a misaligned load): take the MEM-stage
        result = mem_to_reg ? load_data : EX/MEM.alu_result;
     b. producer in WB (MEM/WB, valid & reg_write): wb_w_data (this is
        today's write-first bypass);
     c. regfile read.
   The value is captured in ID/EX flops. dmem stall is safe: stall_id
   already holds ID/EX whenever MEM does not complete, so a load value
   is only ever captured in a cycle where the bus delivered it.
3. EX keeps exactly one bypass, from the instruction directly ahead
   (EX/MEM.alu_result). Its select is computed in ID
   (ID/EX.rd == rs, rd != 0, ID/EX.valid & reg_write) and registered
   in ID/EX as one bit per operand; in EX it is ANDed with the
   registered EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write so a producer that trapped in EX
   (misaligned JAL/JALR target, reg_write cleared) does not forward
   and the consumer falls back to the value resolved in ID. Whenever
   ID/EX captures, the instruction in EX moves into EX/MEM on the same
   edge (dmem stall and ex_busy both hold ID/EX), so the registered
   select always points at the right register; the M unit already
   samples its operands only on its start cycle. The MEM/WB -> EX
   forward leg and the combinational forward_unit in EX disappear.
   Load-use detection is unchanged (LOAD in EX, consumer in ID stalls
   one cycle, then picks the load data up through bypass 2a).
4. Fold the operand-B choice into ID/EX too: register
   alu_b = alu_src ? imm : rs2 and alu_a = is_auipc ? pc : rs1 so the
   EX operand logic is one LUT3 per bit
   (sel_exmem_q & exmem_reg_write ? EX/MEM.alu_result : idex value),
   with rs2 kept separately for store data / branch compare.

The new ID paths (dmem BSRAM -> load align -> bypass mux -> ID/EX, and
lfsr/imem -> LUT-RAM read -> bypass mux -> ID/EX) are short next to
today's EX path, because decode currently has almost a full cycle of
slack in the bench. Expected: EX path loses the BSRAM clock-to-out
delta, the post-BSRAM gating level, one mux level and the WB mux leg,
roughly 22.3 ns -> 17-18.5 ns, i.e. Fmax ~59.8 -> ~66-72 MHz at an
unchanged iteration/cycle. That clears the 4.6% acceptance bar with
margin and leaves ALU-internal restructuring (shared adder, shifter)
as an orthogonal follow-up.

title: Fetch-cycle bimodal predictor (256x2b PHT + JAL always-taken) rebased on the M-unit champion
motivation:
The champion (r1s0, 130.46 iter/s) resolves every branch/jump in EX and
loses one fetch slot per taken branch / JAL / JALR. r1s2 measured a
fetch-cycle predictor at +7.11% iter/cycle on the old baseline but it was
never merged. I rebased it on the champion RTL in a scratch copy and
measured both halves of the fitness (prototype reverted afterwards):
  CoreMark (cosim_sim coremark.elf 50000000 --bench --istall --dstall,
  all 5 CRCs + "Correct operation validated" OK):
    champion   4,585,414 cycles
    prototype  4,287,028 cycles (15,053 -> 4,302,081)  => +6.96% iter/cycle
  Gowin timing, placement option 0 only (make timing TARGET=bench):
    champion   58.851 MHz (p0; p1/p2 59.821, median 59.821), 2353 LUT
    prototype  56.667 MHz (p0), 2595 logic, 573 FF, 24 LUT-RAM, 16 levels
So p0-vs-p0 the prototype is +3.0% fitness (132.2 vs 128.3 iter/s) and
+1.3% against the champion's median. As measured this does NOT clear the
4.6% acceptance bar: the IPC gain is real, but about half of it was
given back in Fmax in the one placement I had time to run. Not measured:
the other two placement options, and whether the -3.7% Fmax is
placement noise or a real cost of the new logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a fetch-cycle predictor; no BTB is needed because IF/ID is a wire and
the instruction is visible in the same cycle as its PC.
1. if_stage: is_jal_f / is_br_f from imem_data[6:0]; imm_f = J-imm or
   B-imm; bj_target = pc + imm_f (dedicated adder). 256x2b PHT
   `logic [1:0] pht [0:255]`, async read at pc[9:2], sync write, `initial`
   2'b01, no reset (maps to LUT-RAM).
   pred_taken = !flush && (is_jal_f || (is_br_f && pht_ctr[1])) && !imm_f[1]
   (flush = imem stall; misaligned targets are never predicted so the
   existing EX trap path is untouched). next_pc = pred_taken ? bj_target
   : pc+4, under the unchanged PC priority reset > redirect > !stall.
   `redirect` must stay out of pred_taken and out of the instr NOP mux
   (r1s0's cut): when redirect=1 ID/EX is flushed or held, so the payload
   is never captured.
2. if_id_t / id_ex_t carry pred_taken + pht_ctr[1:0]; the PHT index is
   in.pc[9:2] in EX.
3. ex_stage: actual = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault;
   redirect = actual != in.pred_taken;
   redirect_target = is_jump ? jump_target
                   : in.pred_taken ? pc+4 : branch_target
   (the target mux selects on registered bits only, never on the
   compare). pc_next / RVFI unchanged. Training: train_en = in.valid &&
   is_branch && !stall, saturating inc/dec of the carried counter.
Timing facts from the prototype run: the 5 worst paths all sit at
22.90-22.94 ns. Four are the existing EX cone (regfile/ID-EX -> fwd ->
ALU -> EX/MEM alu_result -> dmem address), one is regfile -> EX compare
-> redirect -> if_stage pc (13 cells, 22.903 ns), i.e. the mispredict
path is co-critical with the ALU path rather than a new dominant one.
Untested ideas for the implementer to recover Fmax: form redirect as
in.pred_taken ? !actual : actual with the JAL/JALR terms pre-resolved
from registered ctrl bits, and keep the stall terms off the redirect
select at the PC D input. Run all three placement options before
trusting the result. Out of scope: return-address stack (needs a
32-bit target compare behind the forward mux), global history (r1s2:
gshare no better than bimodal), BTB.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-003-r2s2 (regression, +8.83%): The fetch-cycle predictor (JAL always-taken + 256x2b bimodal PHT at pc[9:2], pc+imm adder in if_stage) rebased on r1s0 scored 141.98 against the round-start 130.46 — almost three times its own +3% estimate and above the 4.6% acceptance margin — and is a "regression" only because sibling r2s0 won the same round with 213.91 (one winner per round, highest fitness), so it is now unmerged after two rounds for reasons unrelated to its merit; the estimate was low because it rested on a single option-0 timing run of the prototype (56.667 vs the champion's 58.851 MHz p0), whereas the score implies a ~60.9 MHz median if cycles matched the prototype's 4,287,028 (+6.96% iter/cycle; scribe's inference — no timing report, cycle count or implementer notes reached the scribe), i.e. the full IPC gain with no Fmax cost at ~60 MHz, and the implementation differs from the prototype exactly where the hypothesis asked: instead of `redirect = actual != in.pred_taken` (an XOR behind the 32-bit compare) it expands on the late signal — `redirect = branch_cond ? red_t : red_f` with both arms built from registered ID/EX bits (is_branch, pred_taken, target alignment, the 2-bit JALR sum) — selects `redirect_target` (jump_target / pc+4 / branch_target) on registered bits only, and registers train_en/train_idx/train_ctr in EX so the PHT LUT-RAM write stays off the compare cone (table updated one cycle late); whether those edits or placement luck closed the 56.7 -> ~60.9 MHz gap was not separated, but three things carry over: a one-option prototype Fmax can be wrong by more than a single-digit IPC idea is worth, so size such ideas from the `--all-options` median before trusting or discarding them; a prediction check need not add depth behind the compare when both outcomes are precomputed and the compare is only the last 2:1 select; and an idea capped at ~7% loses every round in which any sibling lands a bigger Fmax win, however orthogonal, and must then be rebuilt on the new champion — so re-propose it on r2s0 when it is the largest remaining gain (or fold it into the slot expected to win), where the same ~298k cycles saved would give ~228.8 (+7.0%) if 98.1 MHz holds and break even at ~91.7 MHz, r2s0's ID-registered `br_ok/br_bad/jal_ok/jal_bad` plus the fetch-time pred_taken would let `red_t`/`red_f` be formed in ID and registered (untested), and what nobody has timed at a ~10 ns period is the fetch side — imem_data -> B/J imm mux -> 32-bit add -> next_pc, and pc[9:2] -> PHT read -> pred_taken -> PC — on top of `redirect` -> PC, which r2s0 already reports as co-critical.

title: Fetch skid buffer: keep fetching during backend stalls so they overlap with imem bus stalls
motivation:
At 98 MHz the champion's two EX path families are tied and the mux-flattening
budget is spent (r2s0 lesson), so this slot goes after iterations/cycle with a
change that stays off the `redirect` cone. CPI is ~1.5 and roughly 18% of all
cycles are imem-stall bubbles (22% iStall). Today every backend stall
(dmem stall with a LOAD/STORE in MEM, load-use bubble, M-unit `ex_busy`) also
freezes the PC: the instruction that imem delivered in that cycle is thrown
away and must be fetched again next cycle, where it is exposed to a fresh 22%
chance of an imem stall. Backend stalls and fetch stalls therefore ADD, when
they could OVERLAP. Backend stall cycles are ~0.15 per instruction
(dStall ~0.08, load-use ~0.04, MUL ~0.03), so letting fetch run one or two
instructions ahead during them hides a later imem stall most of the time.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small fetch skid buffer (shift FIFO, depth 2, head always entry 0) in
if_stage between imem and decode, WITHOUT adding an IF/ID pipeline stage:
when the buffer is empty the imem word still feeds decode combinationally in
the same cycle (taken-branch penalty stays 1 cycle).
  - head instr = buf_v0 ? buf_instr0 : (imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP)
    (a 4-input function per bit = one LUT4, replacing today's NOP mux, so no
    extra logic level in front of the decoder); head pc = buf_v0 ? buf_pc0 :
    fetch_pc; out.valid = (buf_v0 || imem_ready) && !redirect.
  - consume = head valid && ID/EX captures it (!stall_id && !flush_id).
  - fetch_accept = imem_ready && (buffer not full after this cycle's
    consume); fetch_pc advances by 4 on fetch_accept, independent of the
    backend stall. The fetched word is pushed when it is not consumed by the
    bypass in the same cycle.
  - redirect: fetch_pc <= target (still overrides everything), buffer valid
    bits cleared. Only the valid bits join the redirect fan-out; buf_pc /
    buf_instr are plain enable flops, so nothing is added behind the branch
    compare.
hazard_unit keeps computing load-use from the HEAD instruction; the old
stall_if (PC hold on load-use / dmem stall / ex_busy) is replaced by the
buffer-full condition; flush_if (NOP) becomes "head not valid". ID/EX,
EX/MEM, MEM/WB capture conditions are unchanged, so the registered
forwarding-select invariant from r2s0 (ID/EX captures exactly when EX/MEM
and MEM/WB advance by one instruction) is untouched.
MEASURED at hypothesis time (prototype: only if_stage.sv rewritten as above
with DEPTH=2 plus two wiring lines in core.sv; Verilator cosim, --bench
--istall --dstall): CoreMark bracketed cycles 4,585,414 -> 4,386,473
(-4.34% cycles = +4.54% iterations/cycle), all five CRCs and "Correct
operation validated." intact, no oob. Fmax was NOT measured (no time for a
Gowin run): expected flat because the decode path gains no LUT level and the
new enables hang off stall_id, which already drives the PC enable; only the
FIFO count bits join the redirect fan-out. +4.5% is right at the 4.6%
acceptance margin, so Fmax must not drop: score it with
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` (median) and loop on the
timing report if the buffer write-enable or head mux shows up. Extra cycles
are available only from (b) keeping the redirect target in the buffer when
redirect stays asserted for several cycles under a dmem stall (not
measured). Do NOT spend effort on precise load-use (stall only when the head
really reads rs1/rs2): a prototype of it on top of the buffer gave the
identical cycle count (4,386,473; not investigated why).
Orthogonal to and stackable with the unmerged bimodal predictor (~+7%) and
with any EX-cone Fmax work.

title: Decoupled front-end: 2-entry prefetch FIFO hides imem stalls behind backend stalls, plus fetch-time JAL folding
motivation:
Fmax work is at diminishing returns at 98 MHz (two EX path families tie), while
iterations/cycle has never moved: CoreMark still costs 4,585,414 cycles (~1.56
cycles per retired instruction). The bench draws io_imemReady and io_dmemReady
independently every cycle (22% stall each). Today PC and the combinational IF/ID
payload are frozen by every backend stall (stall_if = load_use || imem_stall ||
dmem_stall || ex_busy), so a cycle where imem IS ready but the backend is blocked
(dmem stall with a LOAD/STORE in MEM, load-use bubble, MUL/DIV busy) throws the
delivered word away, and a later cycle where imem is NOT ready starves an idle
backend with a NOP bubble. The two stall sources add up although they could overlap.
Separately, every JAL costs a wasted fetch slot although its target is known from
the instruction word alone.
Prototype measured during hypothesis generation (Verilator cosim, --istall --dstall,
CoreMark CRCs + "Correct operation validated" OK):
  champion                      4,585,414 cycles
  1-entry FIFO                  4,402,146  (+4.16% iter/cycle)
  2-entry FIFO                  4,386,473  (+4.54%)
  2-entry FIFO + JAL fold       4,330,182  (+5.89%)
Gowin timing of the FIFO + JAL-fold prototype (place option 0 only): 100.169 MHz,
10 logic levels, 2570 logic / 710 FF (champion median 98.085), i.e. Fmax is flat and
the predicted score is ~98-100 MHz x (10 / 4,330,182) = 226-231 (+5.9% to +8%).
Worst paths: MEM/WB.alu_result -> EX compare -> redirect -> FIFO data flops
(pc1/i0 clock-enables), and imem_ready -> decoder -> ID/EX.op_b (9 cells), all ~15.27 ns.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple fetch from the backend with a small queue in if_stage and resolve JAL at
fetch time. No predictor state, no speculation beyond what exists today.

(1) Prefetch FIFO (2 entries of {pc, instr}, valid bits v0/v1, empty-bypass):
  - `stall` into if_stage now means "backend cannot consume" =
    load_use || dmem_stall || ex_busy (imem_stall removed from stall_if).
  - fetch_acc = imem_ready && !redirect && (!full || !stall); PC advances on fetch_acc.
  - pop = v0 && !stall; push = fetch_acc && (v0 || stall)  (a word that decode takes
    directly through the bypass is not pushed).
  - out.pc = v0 ? pc0 : pc; out.instr = v0 ? i0 : (imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP);
    out.valid = (v0 || imem_ready) && !redirect.
  - redirect clears v0/v1 and loads PC (overrides everything, as today).
  With the FIFO empty the core is cycle-for-cycle the champion (taken-branch penalty
  stays 1). stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb are unchanged, so ID/EX
  still captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance and the ID-registered
  forwarding selects stay valid. load_use is computed from out.instr (FIFO head or
  live word), which does not depend on `stall`, so there is no combinational loop.

(2) Fetch-time JAL folding: when the live word being accepted is a JAL with an
  aligned target (imem_data[6:0]==1101111 && !jimm[1]; PC is always 4-aligned),
  PC <= pc + jimm instead of pc + 4, so the next fetched word is already the target.
  EX then no longer redirects for JAL (drop `in.jal_ok` from `redirect`, which also
  takes one term off the critical redirect cone); link value, pc_next, and the
  misaligned-JAL trap (jal_bad: no fold, PC stays linear, trap in EX) are unchanged.
  JALR and conditional branches still resolve in EX.

Timing notes from the prototype (100.2 MHz p0): the new worst path is `redirect` into
the FIFO data-flop enables, so make only v0/v1 depend on redirect - write pc0/i0/pc1/i1
with enables built from flops + imem_ready + `stall` (data is don't-care when the
valid bit is cleared). Second is imem_ready -> NOP mux -> decoder -> op_b: gate
only `valid`/reg_write-type control with imem_ready instead of muxing a NOP into the
instr word if that can be shown safe (load_use must still see rs=0 or be gated).
Confirm with `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` (median is scored).

Remove `in.jal_ok` from `redirect` (aligned JAL is already redirected at fetch); keep pc_next = jump_target, link = pc+4, and the jal_bad misalign trap exactly as is.
Wire io_imemReady into if_stage and remove the flush_if connection.

cocotb test of if_stage: FIFO banks words during backend stall, drains across imem stalls, flushes on redirect, never drops/duplicates/reorders under random imem_ready/stall/redirect; aligned JAL folds to pc+jimm, misaligned JAL does not.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-002-r3s1 (improvement, +8.83%): First iterations/cycle win (213.91 -> 232.79; no timing report, cycle count or implementer notes reached the scribe, so the split is inferred: the prototype's 4,585,414 -> 4,330,182 CoreMark cycles, +5.89%, would put the scored median at ~100.8 MHz, i.e. Fmax flat-to-slightly-up vs 98.1) and it came from stall accounting rather than from any predictor state: the bench draws `io_imemReady` and `io_dmemReady` independently at ~22% each, and a PC frozen by every backend stall (load-use, dmem stall with a LOAD/STORE in MEM, `ex_busy`) discards a delivered imem word and re-exposes it to a fresh imem stall, so the two stall sources add — taking imem_stall out of `stall_if` and banking the word in a 2-entry {pc, instr} FIFO with empty-bypass in if_stage (`fetch_acc = imem_ready && !redirect && (!v1 || !stall)`, a word decode takes through the bypass is not pushed, taken-branch penalty still 1) makes them overlap for +4.54%, which sibling r3s0 confirmed to the cycle with an independent FIFO-only build (4,386,473 cycles, 99.09 MHz median of 103.5/99.1/99.1, 225.9, lost this round only by the JAL margin; its scribe timed out so this is its record too); fetch-time folding of aligned JALs (`imem_data[6:0]==1101111 && !imem_data[21]` -> `pc <= pc + jimm`, second adder parallel to pc+4, misaligned JAL left unfolded to trap in EX via `jal_bad`) added the other +1.3% and deleted `in.jal_ok` from the co-critical `redirect` OR, because a JAL target needs only the instruction word and the always-4-aligned PC; it cost no Fmax because `redirect` reaches only v0/v1 and PC while pc0/i0/pc1/i1 are written with enables from valid flops + `stall` (data is don't-care under a cleared valid bit — the prototype's worst path was `redirect` into those data-flop enables), and because stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb are untouched, so r2s0's "ID/EX captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance" invariant for the registered forwarding selects still holds and load-use is read from the FIFO-head-or-live word with no loop through `stall`; title: Fetch-cycle bimodal predictor on the 98 MHz champion with ID-precomputed mispredict selects (zero added depth on redirect)
motivation:
The champion (r2s0, 213.91 iter/s, 98.1 MHz, 4,585,414 CoreMark cycles) has
no branch prediction: every taken branch, JAL and JALR is resolved in EX and
kills the instruction fetched behind it (1 lost fetch slot each). IF/ID is a
wire (the instruction is visible in the same cycle as its PC), so a
fetch-cycle predictor needs no BTB: it pre-decodes imem_data and computes
pc+imm itself.
This idea has been measured twice and never merged, both times only because
a sibling slot won the round with a bigger Fmax gain:
  r1s2 (old baseline)   4,491,485 -> 4,193,175 cycles, +7.11% iter/cycle
  r2s2 (M-unit champ)   4,585,414 -> 4,287,028 cycles, +6.96% iter/cycle,
                        scored 141.98 vs 130.46 (+8.83%), i.e. no Fmax
                        cost at ~60 MHz.
r2s0 changed only Fmax (cycle count is still exactly 4,585,414), so the
same ~298k cycles are available: 98.1 MHz x 10 / 4,287,028 = 228.8 iter/s
(+7.0%). Break-even with the champion is 91.7 MHz; the 4.6% acceptance
bar needs Fmax >= ~95.9 MHz, i.e. the predictor may cost at most ~2%.
NOT measured in this slot (no prototype/timing run fit the 20-minute
budget): Fmax of the predictor at a ~10 ns period. r2s0's worst paths are
(a) MEM/WB value -> rs1/rs2 3:1 mux -> compare -> `redirect` -> flush_id/PC
and (b) fwd_a -> mux -> adder/shifter -> EX/MEM.alu_result, tied at ~10.3 ns
of data. So the design below is shaped so that nothing is added behind the
compare, and the redirect-target path gets shorter than it is today.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a fetch-cycle direction predictor (JAL always taken + 256x2-bit bimodal
PHT for conditional branches, target = pc+imm computed in IF), with every
prediction-dependent decision that EX needs pre-computed in the IF/ID cycle
and registered in ID/EX.

1. Fetch (if_stage):
   - is_jal_f = imem_data[6:0]==7'b1101111, is_br_f = imem_data[6:0]==
     7'b1100011 && imem_data[14:13]!=2'b01 (exclude the reserved funct3
     2/3 encodings, which the decoder traps and which must fall through
     to pc+4). The B/J immediate mux is selected by imem_data[3] alone
     (1 for JAL, 0 for BRANCH; any other opcode never predicts, so its
     imm_f is a don't-care): one LUT level in front of a dedicated 32-bit
     adder bj_target = pc + imm_f. The full opcode decode only gates
     pred_taken, in parallel with the carry chain.
   - PHT: `logic [1:0] pht [0:255]`, async read at pc[9:2], sync write,
     `initial` 2'b01, no reset loop, syn_ramstyle distributed_ram (same
     recipe as the regfile, so it stays LUT-RAM and formal sees free state).
   - pred_taken = imem_ready && (is_jal_f || (is_br_f && pht_ctr[1]))
                  && !imm_f[1]   (pc[1:0] is always 00, so target alignment
     is imm_f[1]; misaligned targets are never predicted and keep the
     existing EX trap path with a linear PC).
   - next_pc = pred_taken ? bj_target : pc+4 under the UNCHANGED PC
     priority reset > redirect > !stall. `redirect` stays out of pred_taken
     and out of the instr NOP mux (r1s0's cut). Invariant that makes this
     safe: ID/EX captures only when !stall_id && !flush_id, and then
     stall_if can only be the imem stall, in which case the payload is a
     NOP with pred_taken=0 - so "pred_taken latched in ID/EX" always means
     "PC really went to bj_target".
2. ID/EX carries (all formed in the IF/ID cycle from instruction bits, the
   fetch-time prediction and tgt alignment; cleared by reset/flush, held on
   stall like the rest of the register):
     red_t   : redirect if the branch condition evaluates TRUE
               = is_branch && tgt_aligned && !pred_taken
     red_f   : redirect if the branch condition evaluates FALSE
               = is_branch && pred_taken
     red_any : non-branch whose fetch-time prediction disagrees with the
               decoder = !is_branch && (pred_taken != (JAL && tgt_aligned))
               (normally 0: covers an unpredicted JAL -> alt_pc = target,
               and anything predicted taken that the decoder does not
               accept as a branch/JAL -> alt_pc = pc+4; kept so correctness
               never depends on the fetch pre-decode matching the decoder)
     alt_pc  : the PC to repair to = pred_taken ? pc+4 : bj_target
               (both already exist in IF; 32 flops)
     pht_ctr[1:0] (index is in.pc[9:2] in EX)
   These replace br_ok / jal_ok in the redirect equation (br_bad / jal_bad
   stay for the misalign trap).
3. EX (ex_stage):
     redirect = (branch_cond ? in.red_t : in.red_f) || in.red_any
                || (in.ctrl.is_jalr && !jalr_sum[1]);
   which has the same number of late inputs and the same LUT depth behind
   cmp_eq / cmp_ltu as today's `(br_ok && branch_cond) || jal_ok || jalr`
   - the prediction just swaps which compare outcome redirects, no XOR is
   appended (r2s2's `branch_cond ? red_t : red_f` trick, now with the
   arms registered). If timing wants it flatter, pre-decode four one-hot
   bits in ID instead (redirect-on-eq / -ne / -lt / -ge) and AND-OR them
   with cmp_eq and (cmp_ltu ^ sign-fix).
     redirect_target = in.ctrl.is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : in.alt_pc;
   i.e. the in.pc + in.imm adder disappears from the timed redirect_target
   cone (it is still needed for RVFI pc_next / branch_target, which is
   verification-only and pruned). JALR is never predicted and behaves as
   today. A correctly predicted taken branch / JAL raises no redirect
   (0 bubbles instead of 1); a branch wrongly predicted taken is repaired
   to pc+4. pc_next, ctrl_with_trap, misalign traps and the EX/MEM
   register are computed from the architectural outcome exactly as now.
4. Training: train_en = in.valid && in.ctrl.is_branch && !stall && !ex_busy
   (once per branch, when EX/MEM accepts it), train_idx = in.pc[9:2],
   train_ctr = saturating inc/dec of in.pht_ctr by branch_cond; all three
   are REGISTERED in EX and written to the PHT one cycle later so the
   LUT-RAM write port is off the compare cone.
5. hazard_unit and forward_unit are untouched: `redirect` still means
   "kill the instruction in IF/ID", and ID/EX still captures exactly when
   EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance by one instruction (r2s0's registered-select
   invariant is preserved because no stall/flush condition changes).

Expected: +7.0% iter/cycle (4,585,414 -> ~4,287,000 cycles; re-measure with
the --bench --istall --dstall cosim, CRCs must match). Fmax target: within
2% of 98.1 MHz. New paths to watch in `make timing` and fix inside the
slot, scored with `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`:
  - imem_data -> imm_f mux -> 32-bit add -> pred mux -> redirect mux -> PC
    and -> ID/EX.alt_pc (if it shows up: use two parallel adders pc+Bimm /
    pc+Jimm, or select alt_pc from registered pc/imm in EX instead);
  - pc[9:2] -> PHT LUT-RAM read -> pred_taken -> 32-bit PC select (if it
    shows up: shrink to 64 entries, which removes two mux levels; CoreMark's
    hot branches are few);
  - `redirect` -> PC: must stay a single 2:1 level in front of the PC flops
    with the stall/predicted mux resolved before it.
If the median Fmax ends below ~96 MHz with no fixable path, report the
measured cycles and Fmax rather than trading away correctness gates.
Out of scope: return-address stack / JALR prediction (needs a 32-bit target
compare behind the forward mux), global history (r1s2: gshare 256 +6.77%,
1024 +7.24% vs bimodal +7.11%), BTB.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-003-r3s2 (regression, -0.89%): The fetch-cycle bimodal predictor rebuilt on the 98 MHz r2s0 champion kept its whole iterations/cycle gain and lost all of it to Fmax — scored 212.00 at a 90.9 MHz median (98.1 -> 90.9, -7.3%; +222 LUT4; formal 53/53 and cosim CRCs clean first try), which is exactly the prototype's 4,287,028 cycles (+6.96%; scribe's inference from 212.00 x 4,287,028 / 10 = 90.9 MHz, the implementer did not record cycles) — because a 1-bubble EX-resolved predictor is worth at most ~7% and so must cost under ~2% Fmax, yet it has to touch the one cone r2s0 left co-critical, forwarded MEM/WB value -> rs1/rs2 mux -> 32-bit compare -> `redirect` -> PC / flush_id, and "zero added LUT depth on paper" did not survive place-and-route there: with the mispredict arms registered in ID/EX (`redirect = branch_cond ? in.red_t : in.red_f`, `redirect_target = in.alt_pc` with no EX adder, PHT training registered) option 0 gave 87.5 MHz with the worst path ID/EX.fwd_rs1 -> compare chain -> four LUT levels of `redirect` -> flush of the ID/EX data flops (40 cells, 16.73 ns), and the hypothesis's own flatter fallback (four one-hot `red_eq/red_ne/red_lt/red_ge` AND-ORed with `cmp_eq` / `cmp_ltu ^ sign-fix`) was worse, 86.0 MHz with MEM/WB.alu_result -> fwd mux -> equality LUT tree folded into `redirect` -> PC clock-enable (10 cells, 16.92 ns) — so both mispredict directions being live behind the compare (redirect on TRUE or on FALSE, versus the champion's taken-only `br_ok && branch_cond` with the invert folded into `cmp_flip`) plus a PC that now selects among redirect_target / pc+imm / pc+4 is enough to cost ~0.7-1.5 ns, and the fetch-side paths the hypothesis worried about (imem_data -> B/J imm mux -> 32-bit add -> PC, pc[9:2] -> PHT read -> pred_taken) never appeared in the top paths; the split between `redirect` logic depth, PC/flush fan-out and placement was not separated (the champion was not re-timed in the worktree, and option 0 sat ~5 MHz under the scored median, a wider spread than r2s0's +/-1.5), but the pattern is now measured at both ends — free at ~60 MHz (r2s2), a wash at ~98 MHz — and r2s0's warning that mux-level re-arrangement of this cone is spent held for the predictor too; consequences: do not re-propose the predictor as an add-on to the single-cycle compare -> `redirect` -> PC loop, and never again without a hypothesis-time `--all-options` timing run (this slot submitted with Fmax explicitly unmeasured, and Fmax was the only thing that decided it); on the new r3s1 champion (232.79, JAL already folded at fetch, 2-entry fetch FIFO) the remaining prize is conditional branches only, roughly +5% (scribe's estimate: 6.96% minus the ~1.3% JAL share, not re-measured), so the affordable Fmax cost is even smaller than the 7.3% lost here; the version worth trying (scribe's inference, untested) pairs the predictor with a structural cut it uniquely pays for — register the mispredict (`redirect`/`redirect_target` flopped out of EX, or resolved in MEM), turning the penalty into 2 slots but only on mispredicts, which the bimodal table makes rare, while every correctly predicted branch costs 0 and compare -> `redirect` leaves the single-cycle PC/flush path altogether (an Fmax gain rather than a cost, since that path is one of the two that tie at the top) — subject to squashing the one extra wrong-path instruction in EX/MEM before it writes or stores, keeping r2s0's "ID/EX captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance" invariant for the registered forwarding selects, and carrying pred_taken/pht_ctr through r3s1's FIFO entries.

title: Take late redirect off the 230-flop ID/EX reset net and imem_ready off the decode cone (narrow kill bits, late-select flush)
motivation:
Measured at hypothesis time on the champion (make timing, place option 0:
93.4 MHz, 12 logic levels; the scored median is 100.8). 24 of the 25 worst
setup paths are ONE family, all within 0.07 ns of each other (15.93-16.00 ns
arrival):
  EX/MEM.alu_result -> rs1/rs2 forward mux (2 LUT) -> 32-bit compare carry
  chain -> 1.70 ns net -> 3 LUT levels of redirect (fan-out 39) -> 0.87 ns
  net -> u_id/n99 = (reset || flush) LUT with FAN-OUT 230 -> 1.05 ns net ->
  synchronous RESET pin of ID/EX *data* flops (rs1_val, rs2_val, imm, op_a,
  op_b, ctrl.alu_op, ...) and the PC flops.
Route is 6.4 ns of the 10.4 ns data path. The 25th path (15.968 ns) is
stall_gen/imem_ready -> NOP mux on out.instr -> decoder/imm_gen -> ID/EX.op_b.
So the clock period is set by a 1-bit decision (kill the wrong-path
instruction in ID) that is implemented as a wide synchronous clear of every
ID/EX flop, fed through 4 LUT levels after the compare chain, plus a NOP mux
that puts a bus-ready flop in front of the whole decoder.
IPC side is nearly exhausted for small edits: cosim shows 2.937M instructions
in 4.330M cycles while imem can deliver at most 0.78125 words/cycle, i.e. the
core is fetch-bound and only a predictor (already tried 3x, Fmax-negative)
can recover cycles. Fmax on this one path family is the micro_opt lever.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three small, mutually reinforcing edits, no change to cycle behaviour
(CoreMark cycles must stay exactly 4,330,182; stall_id / flush_id /
stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb semantics unchanged, so the registered forwarding
selects invariant from r2s0 is untouched):
1. Narrow kill. In id_stage, flush clears ONLY the side-effect bits of ID/EX:
   valid, ctrl.{reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr,
   is_mul, is_div, is_illegal}, br_ok, br_bad, jal_bad (about 13 flops, still
   via `if (reset || flush)` so they keep using the dedicated RESET pin).
   All data/select flops (pc, rs1_val, rs2_val, op_a, op_b, imm, rd, rs?_addr,
   fwd_*, sel_add, alu_op, branch_op, mem_width, instr, ...) lose the reset
   entirely and are written with enable = !stall only. A bubble with
   reg_write = 0, mem_* = 0, br_ok = is_jalr = 0, m_op = 0, valid = 0 has no
   architectural effect whatever its data fields hold (EX/MEM gets ctrl with
   no side effects; forward_unit needs ex_w_en). Fan-out of the late net drops
   from ~270 to ~50, so the placer no longer has to stretch compare -> redirect
   -> every ID/EX slice.

   compare from early (flop or 2-bit-adder) signals and let the compare result

title: Late-select redirect: register EX branch resolve, steer imem address from the flop; bimodal predictor rides on it
motivation:
At 100.8 MHz the worst path is still the single-cycle loop
EX/MEM|MEM/WB value -> rs1/rs2 forward mux -> 32-bit compare -> `redirect`
-> PC / FIFO valids / flush_id (36 cells, 15.999 ns). r2s0 and r3s2 showed
that mux-level rework of this cone is spent, and that a branch predictor
(worth ~+5% iter/cycle for conditional branches now that JAL is folded)
loses 7% Fmax when its mispredict logic sits behind the compare in that
same loop. The scribe's proposed cut (flop the redirect) was assumed to
cost a 2-slot mispredict penalty. It does not have to: the imem contract
is combinational (io_imemAddr -> io_imemData in the same cycle, the fetch
address is only an observed output in the timed netlist), so a REGISTERED
redirect target can be muxed straight onto io_imemAddr in the next cycle.
The target instruction then reaches decode in exactly the cycle it does
today; the one wrong-path instruction is squashed in EX instead of being
flushed in ID. Penalty stays at 1 bubble, and the compare ends in a flop.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Structural cut of the compare -> redirect -> PC/flush loop at zero
cycle cost, plus the predictor that this cut makes affordable.

(1) Registered redirect (ex_stage). EX no longer drives a combinational
`redirect`. It registers
      redir_q    <= redir_d && !stall(dmem) && !redir_q
      redir_pc_q <= in.ctrl.is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],1'b0} : in.alt_pc
where redir_d is the old redirect condition (later: the mispredict
condition) and in.alt_pc is a target computed in ID and held in ID/EX,
so no select of redir_pc_q depends on the compare. redir_q is only set
when the branch really leaves EX (a dmem-stalled branch just retries).

(2) Next cycle (redir_q = 1; the branch/JALR is in MEM, which is never a
memory op, so dmem_stall = 0 and nothing is held):
  - if_stage: pc_eff = redir_q ? redir_pc_q : pc; io_imemAddr = pc_eff;
    the IF/ID payload is the live word at pc_eff (FIFO head ignored),
    v0/v1 clear, PC <= fetch_acc ? pc_eff + step : pc_eff. One
    flop-selected 2:1 mux in front of the address output / PC adders.
  - the wrong-path instruction now in ID/EX is squashed: EX/MEM captures
    a bubble (valid=0, ctrl='0) exactly like the ex_busy bubble; m_op
    (muldiv start), redir_d, ex_w_en (forward_unit) and the load-use
    term id_ex_mem_read are all gated with !redir_q (a flop), so the
    target instruction in ID neither forwards from nor stalls on it.
  - ID/EX captures the target instruction normally (no flush_id needed
    for redirects any more: flush_id = load_use && !dmem_stall).
ID/EX still captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance, so r2s0's
registered forwarding selects stay valid. Taken-branch / JALR penalty
is unchanged (1 bubble), so with (1)+(2) alone CoreMark cycles must stay
~4,330,182 while the 32-bit compare leaves the PC / flush / FIFO loop.

(3) Fetch-time bimodal predictor on top (256 x 2b LUT-RAM PHT indexed by
pc_eff[9:2], B-type pre-decode on the live word like jal_fold). Predict
taken only for aligned targets (instr[8]==0): PC <= pc_eff + bimm on
fetch_acc, sharing one adder with the JAL fold (B/J offset mux) in
parallel with +4. pred_taken (+ the 2-bit counter for training) travels
with the word through the FIFO entries and IF/ID. ID registers
red_t = is_branch && aligned && !pred_taken, red_f = is_branch &&
pred_taken and alt_pc = pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm (one ID adder; EX's
redirect-target adder disappears from the timed logic). EX:
redir_d = (branch_cond ? in.red_t : in.red_f) || (is_jalr && !jalr_sum[1]).
This is the r3s2 expansion, but it now feeds ONE flop instead of PC
enables, FIFO valids and the ID/EX flush fan-out, which is where r3s2
lost its 7%. PHT training is registered in EX (written one cycle late).
Correctly predicted branches cost 0, mispredicts 1 (same as a taken
branch today): saved cycles = taken - mispredicted, measured twice for
this table at about 240k of 4.33M (+5.5% iter/cycle) after removing the
JAL share, and each avoided redirect also keeps the banked FIFO words.
br_bad never has pred_taken, so the misalign trap path is untouched.

(4) Drop the NOP mux from the IF/ID instr payload (imem_ready -> NOP mux
-> decoder -> ID/EX.op_b was the 15.27 ns runner-up): feed the decoder
the raw word and kill the instruction with valid/ctrl gating at the
ID/EX capture (a spurious load-use match on a not-delivered word only
turns a bubble into a bubble).

Checked at hypothesis time: fpga/core_bench_si.sv feeds io_imemData from
an LFSR and sends io_imemAddr only to the observer XOR, and
test/cosim/main.cpp reads imem combinationally from io_imemAddr, so the
flop-selected address mux is legal and short (io_imemAddr must stay a
function of flops only). NOT measured: Fmax. A timing-only prototype of
the registered redirect was started but did not finish inside the
budget, so the Fmax side (two other cones tie near 15.3-15.6 ns) is an
estimate of flat to +3%; the +8% rests mainly on the predictor cycles.

Order of work: (1)+(2) first, check cycles unchanged and formal green,
`make timing`; then (3), then (4); score with --all-options. If the PHT
read behind the pc_eff mux shows up in timing, index it with `pc` and
force pred_taken=0 in the redir_q cycle.

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-002-r4s1 (regression, +6.05%): Keeping the 1-bubble mispredict penalty by late-selecting the registered redirect onto the fetch address (`pc_eff = redir_q ? redir_pc_q : pc` driving `io_imemAddr`, the PC adders and the IF/ID payload, wrong-path instruction squashed in EX) was the wrong trade once a bimodal predictor rides on the same cut: it scored 246.87 at a 98.6 MHz median, i.e. ~3.99M CoreMark cycles (+8.4% iter/cycle vs 4,330,182; scribe's inference from fitness — the implementer never extracted cycles; +223 LUT4, formal 53/53 and cosim clean first try), clears the 4.6% acceptance margin, and is a "regression" only because sibling r4s2 built the same EX-registered redirect and 256x2b PHT with the plain 2-slot penalty (`redirect = redir_q` simply replaces the old combinational `redirect` into PC / v0,v1 / `flush_id`, fetch path otherwise untouched) and merged at 286.61 = 116.1 MHz x 4,051,640 cycles — so the saved mispredict slot was worth only ~57k cycles (~1.4%), because mispredicts + JALR are rare once branches are predicted, while the machinery that saves it cost ~15% Fmax (98.6 vs 116.1), because under a combinational imem contract a "flop-selected 2:1 mux" in front of the fetch address sits at the head of the entire fetch cone even though `io_imemAddr` itself is untimed: the literal version timed 86.5 MHz on option 0 with `redir_q` -> live-word-vs-FIFO-head payload mux -> load-use -> `stall` -> `fetch_acc` -> PC and `redir_q` -> `pc_eff` -> PHT read -> `pred_taken` -> ID `alt_pc` adder on top, and the repairs that brought option 0 back to 94.1 MHz (clear v0/v1 on `redir_set`, the D input of `redir_q`, instead of masking them with the flop; index the PHT with `pc` and force `pred_taken` = 0 in the redirect cycle; move the `alt_pc` adder to EX) re-attached the 32-bit compare to three flops instead of one, leaving five families tied at ~15.9 ns (v0 -> instr mux -> load-use -> `stall` -> PC, 12 cells; `fwd_a` -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result; MEM/WB.alu_result -> forward mux -> compare -> `redir_set` -> v1; v0 -> imm_gen -> ID/EX.imm; imem word -> decoder -> ID/EX.op_b) where r4s2's option 0 topped out at 14.59 ns (107.6 MHz); how the gap splits between the `pc_eff` mux, `redir_set` -> v0/v1 and the dropped NOP mux was not separated (two option-0 runs, no staged (1)+(2)-only build, and Fmax was again unmeasured at hypothesis time — r3s2's rule ignored) — hence: fitness is Fmax x iter/cycle, so once prediction makes an event rare, pay the extra penalty cycle rather than add any select to an every-cycle cone; after a register cut let the redirect flop drive PC / FIFO valids / `flush_id` exactly as the combinational signal did, and never put a redirect-derived select (even a registered one) or its D input in front of the fetch address, the payload mux, the PHT index or the FIFO valids; do not re-propose late-select on the r4s2 champion (its ceiling is that ~1.4%); and removing the `imem_ready` NOP mux only moved the launch point of the decode path from `imem_ready` to the imem data flops (imem word -> decoder -> ID/EX.op_b, 10 cells, 15.88 ns, still tied at the top), so after two losing bundles (r4s0, r4s1) that cut remains unproven in isolation and the decoder -> op_b pre-mux depth itself is the thing to shorten if that path leads on the new champion.

title: Fetch-time bimodal predictor with REGISTERED mispredict redirect (compare leaves the PC/flush loop)
motivation:
Every taken conditional branch still costs one bubble plus the banked FIFO
words, and forwarded value -> 32-bit compare -> `redirect` -> PC / flush_id /
FIFO valids is one of the two path families tied at the top of the timing
report. r3s2 showed that a predictor bolted onto that single-cycle loop
keeps its iter/cycle gain but loses 7% Fmax, because both mispredict
directions become live behind the compare. The predictor is the one feature
that makes it affordable to take the compare OUT of the single-cycle loop:
flop the redirect, pay 2 slots only on mispredicts/JALR, 0 on every
correctly predicted branch.
MEASURED at hypothesis time (prototype of exactly this design, Verilator
CoreMark with --istall --dstall, all five CRCs correct, "Correct operation
validated"): 4,330,182 cycles (champion, re-measured here) -> 4,051,640
cycles = +6.87% iterations/cycle, even though mispredicts and JALR now cost
2 slots instead of 1. Gowin --all-options on the QUICK prototype: 87.2 /
93.5 / 93.5 MHz (median 93.488 -> 230.7, parity with 232.79) with ALL top
paths being the one thing the prototype left unregistered: MEM/WB.alu_result
or ID/EX.fwd_rs2 -> compare -> upd_taken -> PHT write (33-35 cells, 16.0-16.8
ns), and the PHT having been built from FLOPS (pht_RAMREG_*, FF 710 -> 1258,
LUT4 2567 -> 3361, LUT-RAM still 32) because of the EX-side read-modify-
write. The registered redirect itself (-> PC / flush / FIFO valids) is NOT
in the top paths any more. So item (3) below is mandatory, not optional:
register the training and make the PHT a true LUT-RAM (single async read
port at pc[9:2], carry the 2-bit counter with pred_taken through FIFO and
ID/EX, syn_ramstyle distributed_ram, no reset loop), then re-run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` and iterate. Break-even:
the candidate ties the champion at ~94.3 MHz and clears the 4.6% acceptance
bar at >= ~98.7 MHz (champion median 100.8); structurally the change REMOVES
logic from the critical redirect cone rather than adding to it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) Predict in fetch. if_stage pre-decodes the live imem word (as it already
does for JAL folding): br_take = opcode==1100011 && funct3[2:1]!=01 (legal
branch only - an illegal 2/3 funct3 must never be steered) && !instr[8]
(bimm[1]==0, target 4-aligned since PC is always aligned) && PHT[pc[9:2]][1].
256x2b bimodal PHT as LUT-RAM (async read, init 01). On fetch_acc,
PC <= (jal_fold||br_take) ? pc + (jal_fold ? jimm : bimm) : pc+4 - one
pc+imm adder behind a J/B immediate 2:1 mux, in parallel with pc+4.
pred_taken rides in the FIFO entries (pt0/pt1, written with the same enables
as i0/i1), in if_id_t (v0 ? pt0 : imem_ready && br_take) and in ID/EX.
(2) Resolve in EX, redirect from flops. EX computes
  mispredict = !redir_q && ( in.br_ok && (branch_cond != in.pred_taken)
                           || in.ctrl.is_jalr && !jalr_sum[1] )
  mp_target  = jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],0} : in.pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm
and registers redir_q <= mispredict && !stall (only when the branch really
moves to MEM), redir_target_q <= mp_target. `redirect`/`redirect_target`
out of ex_stage are those flops. In the redirect cycle the branch is in MEM
(never a memory op -> dmem_stall is 0), PC loads, FIFO valids clear, ID/EX is
flushed by the unchanged flush_id, and the single wrong-path instruction now
in EX is killed: EX/MEM takes a bubble (`if (ex_busy || redir_q)`),
m_op is gated with !redir_q so muldiv never starts on it, and its own
mispredict is gated by !redir_q. No new stall reasons: stall_id / flush_id /
stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb equations are untouched, so the "ID/EX captures
exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance" invariant behind the registered
forwarding selects holds. RVFI pc_next keeps the architecturally resolved
value (unchanged expression).
(3) Train the PHT once per resolved aligned branch (in.br_ok && !redir_q &&
!stall) at in.pc[9:2] with a saturating +/-1. The prototype did a
read-modify-write straight from EX; the real implementation should register
{idx, old ctr (carried from fetch or re-read), outcome} and write a cycle

lesson: - 2026-11-24 hyp-20261124-003-r4s2 (improvement, +23.12%): The bimodal predictor finally merged, after three unmerged rounds (r1s2, r2s2, r3s2), because it was paired with the register cut that only it can pay for, and about two thirds of the win was Fmax rather than prediction — scored 286.61 = 116.1 MHz median x 4,051,640 CoreMark cycles (Fmax 100.8 -> 116.1, +15.2%; cycles 4,330,182 -> 4,051,640, +6.87%, identical to the prototype; LUT4 2567 -> 2788, FF 710 -> 764; formal 53/53 and cosim clean first try) against a +7% forecast — since the two halves cancel each other's cost: a predictor alone puts both mispredict directions behind the 32-bit compare inside the single-cycle `redirect` -> PC / `flush_id` / FIFO-valid loop (r3s2, -7.3% Fmax) and a flopped redirect alone would charge 2 slots on every taken branch, but together a correctly predicted branch costs 0, only mispredicts and JALRs pay the second slot (the whole iter/cycle gain survived a doubled penalty), and the compare ends in one flop (`redir_q <= mispredict && !stall`, target in `redir_target_q`, `pred_taken` folded into the ID-registered inverts as `cmp_ltu ^ (cmp_flip ^ pred_taken)` / `cmp_eq ^ (branch_op[0] ^ pred_taken)` so `br_miss` is no deeper than `branch_cond`), with that flop driving PC / v0,v1 / `flush_id` exactly as the combinational signal did, the one wrong-path instruction in EX squashed by `redir_q` (EX/MEM bubble, `m_op` gated so muldiv never starts, no mispredict or training of its own) and stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb untouched, so r2s0's "ID/EX captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance" invariant still holds; the forecast under-called by 24% because the hypothesis-time prototype's 93.5 MHz median was set entirely by a shortcut the final design removed — an EX-side PHT read-modify-write, which made Gowin build the 256x2b table from flops (FF 1258, LUT4 3361) and put compare -> `upd_taken` -> PHT write on top — and the table infers as LUT-RAM (32 -> 48 cells) only with ONE async read port (`pc[9:2]`), the 2-bit counter carried with the instruction (`ct0/ct1` in the fetch FIFO, `pred_ctr` in ID/EX) instead of re-read, a registered write (`upd_en_q/upd_taken_q/upd_idx_q/upd_ctr_q`, saturating +/-1 on the write cycle), `initial` fill, `syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram"` and no reset loop, the possibly-stale carried counter costing zero cycles; hence: price an IPC feature together with the structural cut it makes affordable (a ~7% feature bought a 15% Fmax cut that three reshuffles of the same cone — r2s0's control-only flush, r3s2, r4s0 — could not), treat a prototype's Fmax as a floor when all its top paths are one known unfinished detail but still run `--all-options` on it (that run is what turned registered training from optional into mandatory), and expect no single next target — option 0 (107.6 MHz, 9 levels; the only option the implementer ran, and again ~7% under the scored median, as 93.4 vs 100.8 was on the previous champion) shows five unrelated families within 0.04 ns at 14.55-14.59 ns: `fwd_a` -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result (9 cells), EX/MEM.alu_result -> u_ex -> forward_unit -> ID/EX.fwd_rs1 (8 cells; presumably forwarded rs1 -> `jalr_sum[1]` misalign trap -> `ex_w_en` -> select compare, scribe's reading of the hierarchy), `alu_op` -> EX/MEM.alu_result (8), the new fetch loop `pc` -> PHT read (RAM16 + 16:1 mux) -> `br_take`/`steer` -> PC (9) and `imem_ready` -> NOP mux -> decoder -> ID/EX.op_b (6), the compare/redirect being gone from the list, so a fix to any one family is worth ~0 unless the others move with it, and which one leads on the median option is unmeasured (implementer's untested candidates for the fetch loop: a 64/128-entry PHT or a registered PHT read); do not re-propose the predictor, the registered redirect or (per r4s1) a 1-bubble late-select, and count mispredicts and JALRs in cosim before sizing a RAS / BTB / better direction predictor — each now costs 2 slots, neither was counted, and gshare already measured no better than bimodal (r1s2); harness gotchas that cost this slot several runs: for this nret=1 core `make cosim` builds the NRET=2 harness and bare `bash formal/run_all.sh` lacks RTL_DIR/CORE_NAME, so use `python3 -m tools.eval.cosim . bench` / `python3 -m tools.eval.formal . bench` (binary via `NRET=1 bash test/cosim/build.sh`), cosim_sim takes maxcycles positionally before the flags (`cosim_sim coremark.elf 50000000 --bench --istall --dstall`), and neither the regfile nor the PHT has a reset, so cocotb programs must initialise every register they read.

title: Flop-launch the late control cones: JALR-misalign via registered redirect, ID-predecoded ALU one-hots, registered MEM byte-mask, divider pre/post regs, late imem_ready gating
motivation:
Measured at hypothesis time on the r4s2 champion (286.61 = 116.1 MHz x
4,051,640 cycles), instrumented cosim, bench region only: 2,922,015
retired instructions in 4,051,639 cycles. The imem bus delivers at most
0.78 words/cycle, so the floor is 3.75M cycles: ALL remaining
iterations/cycle headroom is ~8%, and it is split over events whose
bubbles already overlap imem stalls (541k fetch-starved cycles, 195.5k
load-use bubbles, 94k MUL bubbles of which only 34.5k are followed by a
consumer, 192k dmem-stall cycles, 58,024 redirects = 44,289 branch
mispredicts + 13,735 JALR, 0 divides). No IPC micro-opt is worth >1%,
so a micro_opt can only clear the 4.6% bar through Fmax.
The champion's option-0 report (107.6 MHz) is a wall: 25 paths within
0.16 ns, 62% routing, 8-9 LUT levels. Reading the paths cell by cell,
about two thirds of the wall is NOT the forward-mux -> adder/shifter
datapath but control that is still computed late in EX/MEM/IF and could
be a flop:
 - path 2/11: EX/MEM.alu_result -> 2-LUT rs1 fwd mux -> jalr_sum[1]
   carry -> misalign_jump/ex_w_en -> 2 LUTs in forward_unit ->
   ID/EX.fwd_rs1 / fwd_a (8-9 levels) - exists only so a misaligned
   JALR (never happens in real code) does not forward its link value.
 - path 3: ID/EX.alu_op -> a fan-out-34 op-decode LUT (1.97 ns net in,
   1.44 ns out) -> shifter -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
 - paths 9/18/19/23: divider |a|,|b| negation behind the forward muxes
   and quotient/remainder sign fix-up in front of the EX result mux -
   for an instruction CoreMark executes zero times.
 - path 15: EX/MEM.alu_result[1:0] -> byte mask / misalign -> dmem WEn.
 - paths 5/7/13/20/22: stall_gen imem_ready -> NOP mux -> decoder ->
   ID/EX.op_b, and -> load-use compare -> stall -> fetch_acc -> PC/v0/v1.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Remove every one of those late control cones in one slot by launching
them from flops (the rule that produced r2s0 and r4s2: compute early and
register, do not reshuffle muxes). No stage, stall or flush condition
changes for legal code, so cycles must stay 4,051,640 (+-0).
(A) Misaligned JALR goes through the existing registered redirect:
`mispredict` gets `in.ctrl.is_jalr` (no `!jalr_sum[1]`), with mp_target
= pc+4 when jalr_sum[1] (trap, reg_write cleared, pc_next = pc+4 exactly
as today). The instruction behind it is then squashed by redir_q and
refetched, by which time the trapped JALR is in MEM/WB with reg_write=0.
forward_unit can therefore use the plain ID/EX.ctrl.reg_write FLOP for
the EX-writer compare (jal_bad already known in ID: fold it into that
flop), deleting the alu_result -> fwd mux -> adder -> ex_w_en leg.
(B) Decode the ALU op in ID and register one-hot is_and/is_or/is_xor/
is_lui/is_slt/is_sltu/is_sll/is_sr/sra/sub bits in ID/EX; alu.sv takes
them as inputs (5-bit alu_op kept only for the unit-test port).
(C) muldiv: divide gets a registered pre-step (latch raw a/b on start,
take |a|,|b| from flops next cycle) and a registered post-step (sign
fix-up into res_q), so `result` for DIV/REM is a flop and the forward
muxes no longer feed two 32-bit negators. +2 cycles per divide, zero in
CoreMark. MUL timing/latency unchanged; ALTOPS branch unchanged.
(D) EX computes the store byte mask, read/write enables and the
mem-misalign bit from jalr_sum[1:0] + mem_width (low adder bits, early)
and registers them in EX/MEM; mem_stage drives io_dmemWEn/REn and
mem_w_en straight from flops.
(E) imem_ready becomes a last-level gate: IF/ID instr = v0 ? i0 :
imem_data (no NOP mux); id_stage ANDs in.valid into the side-effect
control bits at capture; load-use is compared on the raw word and ANDed
with valid; op_b/fwd_b select uses a 4-input opcode pre-decode
(OP vs everything else) instead of the full legality decoder's alu_src.
NOT included: shrinking the PHT to shorten pc -> PHT -> steer -> PC.
Measured in cosim: 128 entries = 4,079,062 cycles (+0.68%), 64 entries
= 4,072,506 (+0.51%); only do it if that loop alone leads the median
report and buys >1% Fmax.
What stays is the true datapath (fwd mux -> adder/shifter/compare ->
EX/MEM / redir_q); with ~15 of the 25 wall paths gone the placer can
spend its 62% routing share on that. Score on the --all-options median
and iterate on the report inside the slot; formal must keep passing the
misaligned-JALR trap, pc_fwd and liveness checks after (A).
