EX-writer compare uses the registered ID/EX reg_write (jal_bad folded in at ID); no late kill input.
Register one-hot ALU op bits and jal_bad-qualified reg_write; AND in.valid into side-effect controls; fast opcode pre-decode for the op_b / fwd_b select.
Accept pre-decoded one-hot op inputs for the AND-OR result mux and shifter gates; keep the alu_op-driven `out` for unit tests.
Divider: registered operand-abs pre-step and registered sign-fix post-step (DIV/REM +2 cycles); MUL and ALTOPS paths unchanged.
Drive dmem_wen/dmem_ren/mem_w_en and the trap bit from the EX/MEM-registered mask, enables and misalign flag.
Drop the imem_ready NOP mux from the IF/ID instr payload (valid carries it); PHT left at 256 entries.
Load-use compare on the raw head word, gated by its valid bit in the last level.
Add ALU one-hot fields to id_ex_t and byte-mask / enable / misalign fields to ex_mem_t.
Wire the registered reg_write to forward_unit and the head-word valid to hazard_unit.
Update expected DIV/REM latency (36 cycles) while keeping all bit-exact result vectors.
Add a misaligned-JALR case: traps, link register not written, next instruction sees the old register value and executes once.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261124-001-r5s0 (regression, +0.27%): Launching every late CONTROL cone from a flop worked mechanically and bought nothing on the scored median — 287.39 = 116.44 MHz (114.9/116.4/116.4) x 4,051,640 CoreMark cycles (unchanged, measured), LUT4 2788 -> 2765, FF 764 -> 870, formal 53/53 and cosim clean, +0.27% against the 4.6% bar — because the path list it was sized from was the champion's option-0 report (107.6 MHz, the placement outlier ~7% under the median, exactly what r4s0 warned about) and Fmax was once more unmeasured at hypothesis time: with a misaligned JALR routed through `redir_q` (so forward_unit compares against the plain ID/EX `reg_write` flop, `jal_bad` folded in at ID), ALU one-hots decoded in ID and registered (`alu_dp`), the divider's |a|,|b| and sign fix-up registered (+2 cycles per DIV, 0 in CoreMark), byte mask / `dmem_wen` / `dmem_ren` / misalign trap registered in EX/MEM, and the `imem_ready` NOP mux replaced by valid-gating of the side-effect bits at ID/EX capture plus a 4-bit opcode pre-decode for op_a/op_b, none of those cones appears in any timing report any more and option 0 rose 107.6 -> 111.0 -> 114.9 MHz, but the median options were already set by true datapath — A-E exactly as specified measured a 113.05 MHz median (111.0/113.05/113.05, BELOW the champion's 116.12) with four families inside 0.02 ns at ~14.13 ns arrival (~8.8 ns of data after 5.33 ns clock insertion): forward mux -> adder/shifter -> EX result AND-OR -> EX/MEM.alu_result (9 levels), forward mux -> 32-bit compare chain -> `redir_q`, `pc` -> PHT read -> `pc` (11 cells) and v0 -> instr mux -> imm_gen -> ID/EX.imm (8 levels), joined in the submitted build by muldiv DSP product (`prod_*`, ~2.2 ns clock-to-out) -> EX result AND-OR -> alu_result (8 levels, 13.88 ns, top path on all three options) — so deleting ~15 of 25 near-critical paths does not let the placer "spend the freed routing" on the rest: a tied wall moves only when EVERY family in it moves, and the ones left are exactly those a flop-launch cannot touch; the only edit that raised the median was on the datapath tail and not in the hypothesis — run 1 showed four LUT levels between the compare carry chain and the `redir_q` D pin (whether part (A)'s JALR term added them or the champion already had them was not checked), and folding the invert / prediction / `br_ok` / `!redir_q` / `!stall` / JALR terms into two early candidates selected by the chain output (`redir_d = cmp_sel ? red_p1 : red_p0`) took 113.05 -> 116.44 (one run each; scribe's reading: late-select can pay when the endpoint is a single flop, unlike r3s2/r4s0 where the same form fanned out to PC/flush) — while two attempts at the new multiplier-product path each lost ~5% and were reverted (explicit `sel_m ? m_result : ...` mux on a new ID/EX flop: 110.8 MHz, +80 LUT, adder paths back on top; `syn_keep` to make the M result join last: 110.1 MHz, adder path grew to 10 levels), i.e. small edits to the EX result AND-OR swing the median by 110-116 MHz, more than any single remaining idea is worth, so do not hand-force that cone's mapping and treat anything under ~5% as unresolvable without its own `--all-options` run; consequences: do not re-propose control-cone cleanup as an Fmax win on its own (A-E is verified, cycle-neutral and UNMERGED, so the champion still has those cones — fold them in only underneath a change that shortens all the datapath families at once, where they would otherwise resurface as the next tie), read the next target from the median-option report rather than option 0, and size IPC ideas from the counts instrumented for this slot on the champion — 2,922,015 instructions in 4,051,639 bench cycles against a ~3.75M-cycle floor (imem delivers at most 0.78 words/cycle, so ALL remaining iter/cycle headroom is ~8% and much of it overlaps imem stalls): 541k fetch-starved cycles, 195.5k load-use bubbles, 192k dmem-stall cycles, 94k MUL bubbles (only 34.5k with a consumer behind them; registering the product is the implementer's untried fallback at about +2.3% cycles), 58,024 redirects at 2 slots each (44,289 branch mispredicts + 13,735 JALR, so a perfect direction predictor is worth at most ~2.2% and a perfect RAS/BTB ~0.7%), 0 divides, and a 128- / 64-entry PHT measured +0.68% / +0.51% cycles — which leaves (scribe's inference) no single micro_opt on either axis likely to clear 4.6% on this champion; implementer's untested lead for the ID family is an imm_gen format pre-decode from `instr[6:2]` (imm is don't-care for non-immediate opcodes).

title: Two-source front-end: 256-entry in-core instruction replay store feeds fetch when imem stalls (breaks the 0.78 word/cycle fetch ceiling)
motivation:
The champion (116.1 MHz x 4,051,640 cycles) is fetch-bound, not
backend-bound. Measured at hypothesis time with the champion RTL:
CoreMark retires 2,922,016 instructions between the markers, CPI 1.387,
while the bench stalls io_imemReady ~22% of cycles, so a front-end whose
only source is imem has a hard floor of 1/0.78 = 1.28 CPI. Everything
else (load-use, dmem stalls, 2-slot mispredicts/JALR, MUL) together is
only ~0.1 CPI and already overlaps with imem stalls through the 2-entry
FIFO (deepening it measured +0.38%). On the Fmax side r4s2 reports five
unrelated path families tied within 0.04 ns, so no single cut is worth
the 4.6% margin. The one large lever left is structural: give fetch a
SECOND source of instruction words so an imem stall stops being a bubble.
ARCHITECTURE.md explicitly allows logic that hides stalls (it is timed),
CLAUDE.md allows caches, and nobody has tried it (no cache/replay entry
in log.jsonl).
Hypothesis-time prototype (behavioural, in if_stage only, CoreMark
"Correct operation validated", same 2,922,016 retired instructions):
  entries  cycles      iter/cycle
  champion 4,051,640   -
  32       3,764,397   +7.63%
  64       3,719,362   +8.93%
  256      3,567,206   +13.58%
  1024     3,535,956   +14.58%
Fmax was NOT measured (no time for a Gowin run) - see the timing plan.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure if_stage into a two-source fetch. A 256-entry direct-mapped
replay store indexed by pc[9:2] (same index as the PHT) records every
word imem delivers: {tag = pc[31:10], instr[31:0]} in distributed
LUT-RAM (one async read port at pc, one synchronous write port, `initial`
fill, syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram", NO reset loop - the recipe that
made the PHT infer as RAM16 in r4s2) plus 256 valid flops (cleared on
reset; optionally on a decoded FENCE so the store stays architecturally
invisible). Write: `if (imem_ready) store[pc[9:2]] <= {pc[31:10],
imem_data}` (pc and imem_data are what the champion already has; write
port must be registered-input only, never fed by redirect).
Read: rs_hit = valid[idx] && tag[idx] == pc[31:10]. Then
  fhave     = imem_ready || rs_hit
  fw        = imem_ready ? imem_data : rs_word
  fetch_acc = fhave && !redirect && (!v1 || !stall)
and fw replaces imem_data in the pre-decode (jal_fold / br_ok / fimm),
in the FIFO data writes (i0/i1/pt/ct) and in the payload. That is the
whole prototype: backend, redirect flop, flush_id/stall_id, hazard_unit,
forwarding selects and the PHT are untouched, so r2s0's "ID/EX captures
exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance" invariant is unaffected. A
replayed word is bit-identical to what imem would have delivered at that
pc, so RVFI/cosim see no difference; riscv-formal has no imem
consistency check and symbolic imem words stay legal instructions to
retire (the store only replays a word the solver itself supplied).

Timing plan (the acceptance budget: +13.58% iter/cycle clears the 4.6%
margin as long as the scored median stays >= ~107 MHz, i.e. up to -8%
Fmax is affordable; run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`,
not option 0 alone). Three new cones, in order of risk, with the fix to
apply if each shows up at the top:
(1) pc -> RAM16 + 16:1 mux -> decoder -> ID/EX.op_b. Do NOT put rs_word
    on the empty-FIFO bypass leg unless timing proves it free: the
    `imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP` leg in front of the decoder is already
    a tied-critical family. Timing-safe structure: a replayed word always
    ENTERS THROUGH THE FIFO (push when rs_hit && !imem_ready even if the
    FIFO is empty and the backend is idle; out.instr/out.valid/
    out.pred_* keep the champion's imem_ready-only bypass leg), so the
    store's read data ends in i0/i1 flops. Cost: one bubble the first
    time imem stalls with the FIFO empty, after which the FIFO runs one
    word ahead until the next redirect. MEASURED at hypothesis time
    (256 entries, `push = fetch_acc && (v0 || stall || !imem_ready)`,
    out.* bypass leg on imem_ready only): 3,605,513 cycles = +12.37%
    iter/cycle, CoreMark validated - i.e. the timing-safe structure
    keeps all but 1.2% of the bypass variant's +13.58%; with it the
    acceptance threshold is a ~108 MHz median. Start from this variant.
(2) pc -> tag RAM16 + 16:1 mux -> 22-bit compare -> rs_hit -> fetch_acc
    -> PC enable / v0,v1. Build the compare on a carry chain or as a
    2-level LUT tree, keep rs_hit out of everything except PC enable,
    push and v0/v1 D (FIFO data enables stay valid-flops + stall only, as
    r3s1 requires). If it still leads: shorten the tag by only storing
    PCs whose upper bits are zero (pc[31:16] == 0 detected from the pc
    flops in parallel with the RAM read, tag = pc[15:10]); PCs outside
    the window simply never hit. Fallback of last resort: 64 entries
    (RAM16 + 4:1 mux, still +8.9%).
(3) fw -> pre-decode -> steer -> PC, on top of the tied pc -> PHT ->
    br_take -> steer -> PC loop. Store two pre-decoded bits per entry
    (jal_fold, br_ok) next to the word and form
    steer = imem_ready ? (jal_l | br_l & pht_rd[1]) : (jal_r | br_r &
    pht_rd[1]) so the live path gains at most a mux select, and use a
    second parallel pc + imm adder for the replayed word selected late
    (as pc+4 / pc+fimm already are) instead of a mux in front of the
    adder.
Area: ~54 bits x 256 = ~216 RAM16SDP4 + read muxes + 256 FF, well inside
the 10,000 LUT4 budget (2,788 now).

Fmax 116.1 -> 71.7, -38%, against a ~103 MHz tie / ~108 MHz acceptance threshold; LUT4 2788 -> 4796, FF 764 -> 1027, LUT-RAM 48 -> 224; formal 53/53 and cosim clean first try) — because an ASYNC-read distributed-RAM table addressed by the PC flops and read inside the single-cycle PC loop is priced by its WIDTH (address fan-out and route), not by its LUT depth: the hypothesis reused the PHT recipe (256x2b, whose `pc` -> RAM16 + 16:1 mux -> steer -> PC read is already one of the champion's tied families) for a 44-bit entry ({tag `pc[19:10]`, jal_fold, br_ok, instr}), which did infer as LUT-RAM (176 RAM16SDP4, no flops) but hangs `pc[9:2]` on every RAM16 read port, on every write port too (the synchronous write is addressed by the same pc flops), on 44 16:1 read muxes and on the 256-valid-flop mux/decode, so in the only report the implementer ran (option 0, 69.3 MHz, 12 levels) `pc_4` has fan-out 664 and its net to one RAM16 address pin costs 5.24 ns by itself (cells spread from row 18 to row 51) — 61% of the champion's whole 8.6 ns period before the RAM read (0.5 ns), the 16:1 mux (~2.3 ns with route), the replayed-immediate select, the third `pc + fimm_r` carry chain and the PC mux, the top five paths all being `pc_4` -> `pc_2x/3x` at ~19.7 ns arrival (~14.4 ns of data); (b) for a structural idea whose break-even needs Fmax within -8%, synthesize at least the bare table + read mux on the champion before spending a slot, because a 36 MHz gap cannot be iterated away in a slot that fits one timing run; title: Fetch-time return prediction (4-entry RAS, checked in EX against the next-PC already in IF) with all predictor state read from flops
motivation:
Measured at hypothesis time on the r4s2 champion (instrumented copy of
ex_stage, CoreMark 10 iterations, --istall --dstall, 2,937,036 retired
instructions in 4,051,640 bracketed cycles):
  conditional branches 532,346 (taken 295,904), mispredicts 44,661 (8.4%,
    only 6,505 of them from a weak counter, i.e. mostly data-dependent)
  JALR 13,794, of which 13,772 are plain returns `jalr x0, 0(ra)`;
    indirect calls: 0. An ideal 4-entry return stack predicts 13,760 of
    the 13,772 (99.9%).
Every one of those events costs 2 fetch slots since the registered
redirect, so redirects total ~117k cycles (2.9%). Returns are 27.5k of
those cycles (0.68%) and are the only part that is almost perfectly
predictable; gshare already measured no better than bimodal (r1s2), so
the direction side is saturated. The imem bus caps the core at 0.78
words/cycle (2.937M / 0.78 = 3.77M cycles floor), so the whole remaining
iter/cycle headroom is ~7% and the predictor's share is this one.
Honest sizing: the iter/cycle part alone is +0.7%, below the 4.6% bar;
the rest has to come from Fmax, and two of the five path families tied at
the top of r4s2's report are predictor / JALR logic that this change
removes: `pc -> PHT RAM16 + 16:1 mux -> br_take -> steer -> PC` and
`forwarded rs1 -> jalr_sum[1] misalign -> ex_w_en -> forward_unit ->
ID/EX.fwd_*`. Adding a third PC source (the RAS top) without first taking
the PHT read out of the PC loop would make the first of those worse.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three coupled edits, all in the fetch-time predictor and the JALR resolve.

(1) Return-address stack in if_stage (4 x 30-bit flops + 2-bit pointer,
speculative, no repair). On fetch_acc of the live word:
  push pc+4          when the word is JAL or JALR with rd in {x1, x5}
  pop, PC <= ras_top when the word is `jalr x0, 0(x1|x5)` (imm == 0)
A predicted return sets the existing pred_taken bit, which already rides
in pt0/pt1, IF/ID and ID/EX; id_stage registers ret_pred = pred_taken &&
is_jalr. Nothing else is carried: while the JALR sits in EX the IF/ID
bundle pc (v0 ? pc0 : pc) is by construction the address fetch steered
to (FIFO head, or the PC register if the successor is not fetched yet),
so EX checks  rs1[31:2] == if_id.pc[31:2] && !rs1[1].  Only imm==0
returns are predicted, so there is no adder in front of the compare: it
is forwarded rs1 -> 30-bit equality -> redir_q, the depth of today's
cmp_eq -> br_miss -> redir_q (not among the top paths). Correct => no
redirect, 0 slots. Wrong, or an unpredicted JALR => registered redirect
exactly as today (2 slots). Wrong-path pushes/pops (about one accepted
wrong-path word per mispredict) only cost an ordinary redirect later.
Expected 4,051,640 -> ~4,024,000 cycles.

(2) Registered PHT read. Replace the asynchronous pht[pc[9:2]] inside the
PC loop by a 2-bit flop pht_q plus 8-bit pidx_q, loaded whenever PC
changes (enable = fetch_acc || redirect) from pht[pc[9:2]] of the word
being accepted, i.e. the table is indexed by the PREVIOUS fetch address.
For a branch reached sequentially this is the same one-entry-per-branch
bimodal table shifted by one slot. Because the index is no longer
derivable from the branch's own pc, the 8-bit index is carried with the
counter (FIFO entries, IF/ID, ID/EX) and upd_idx_q takes it instead of
in.pc[9:2]. Still ONE read port, registered write, initial fill, no
reset loop, so it stays LUT-RAM. br_take = br_ok && pht_q[1] is then a
flop AND the imem pre-decode, and the PC next-state mux (pc+4 / pc+fimm /
ras_top, redirect on top) is selected by pre-decode bits only. Do NOT mux
the read index with redirect (r4s1); the carried index keeps training
consistent whatever was read. Gate: CoreMark cycles with (2) alone must
stay within ~0.2% of 4,051,640; if the previous-PC index costs accuracy,
drop (2) and keep the async read.

(3) Take the JALR misalign bit out of the forwarding-select cone. A JALR
whose target is misaligned (rs1+imm bit 1) still traps with pc_wdata =
pc+4 and no rd write, but now also raises the registered redirect to
pc+4. The instruction behind it is then squashed in EX and re-fetched,
and decodes when the trapped JALR is already in WB with reg_write = 0, so
forward_unit's ex_w_en can be the pure flop
in.ctrl.reg_write && !in.jal_bad. This costs nothing on CoreMark (no
misaligned jumps) and keeps r2s0's invariant: stall_id / flush_id /
stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb are untouched.

Verification notes: predictions are only hints; every steered PC is
validated in EX against the real rs1, so arbitrary RAS / PHT contents
(formal's symbolic initial state) cannot change architectural results.
Run python3 -m tools.eval.formal . bench and python3 -m tools.eval.cosim
. bench, then python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options and read
the median option, not option 0.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261124-003-r5s2 (regression, -2.89%): The 4-entry fetch-time RAS delivered exactly its counted prize and that prize is too small to survive place-and-route — 278.34 = 111.87 MHz median (110.0/111.9/111.9) x 4,019,300 CoreMark cycles (measured; -0.80% vs 4,051,640, 4.8k cycles better than an ideal RAS alone; Fmax 116.12 -> 111.87, -3.7%; LUT4 2788 -> 2966, FF 764 -> 911; formal 53/53 and cosim clean first try) — because CoreMark has only ~13.8k returns (27.5k of 4.05M cycles) and the Fmax half of the plan was "remove two of the five tied path families", which did happen (`pc` -> PHT RAM16 + 16:1 mux -> steer -> PC and rs1 -> `jalr_sum[1]` -> `ex_w_en` -> forward_unit are gone from the top paths of all three options) yet raised nothing, the same result sibling r5s0 got in the same round: the median option is still walled at ~8.9 ns of data by `fwd_b`/`op_b` -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result (9 cells), `imem_ready` -> decoder/imm_gen -> ID/EX.op_b (8) and MEM/WB.alu_result -> forward mux -> muldiv `dvs_q` operand regs (8), now ~0.3 ns slower than the champion's 8.6 ns with ~180 LUT4 / ~150 FF of new fetch-side state (120 RAS flops, 8-bit PHT index in both FIFO entries, IF/ID and ID/EX) placed around them (scribe's inference — the champion was not re-timed in the slot and no edit was timed alone), while three functionally equivalent builds scored medians of 104.3 (4x30 LUT-RAM RAS, 10 levels), 108.3 (flop RAS, 32-bit PC) and 111.9 MHz (flop RAS, 30-bit `pc_q`, shipped), i.e. equivalent-RTL placement spread on this design is about +/-3.5%, several times the feature's whole gain; so do not re-propose return / indirect-target prediction (measured ceiling +0.80%; direction mispredicts are data-dependent and gshare is no better, so the predictor category is spent on this champion) or any iter/cycle idea smaller than that spread unless a hypothesis-time `--all-options` prototype shows the median itself rising — this slot was submitted at a self-estimated +2% against a 4.6% bar with nothing prototyped or timed, and deleting some families of a tied wall has now measured ~0 twice; what is verified, cycle-proven and UNMERGED, to fold in only underneath a change that shortens the EX/ID datapath families: checking a steered return in EX as `in.ret_pred && rs1[31:2] == if_id.pc[31:2] && !rs1[1]` (while the JALR is in EX the IF/ID pc — FIFO head or PC register — is the address fetch steered to, so no predicted target is carried and, for imm == 0 returns, no adder precedes the compare), a registered PHT read indexed by the PREVIOUS fetch address (`pht_q`/`pidx_q` loaded on `fetch_acc || redirect`, index carried beside the counter into `upd_idx_q`, never muxed with the redirect target) that takes the table out of the PC loop at no accuracy cost (not isolated), a misaligned JALR routed through `redir_q` to pc + 4 so `ex_w_en = in.ctrl.reg_write && !in.jal_bad` is flops only (also r5s0's edit A), and a 30-bit PC register; gotcha for any new fetch-side state: a data enable on `fetch_acc` hangs `imem_ready` -> load-use -> `stall` -> `fetch_acc` on every new flop's CE (120 RAS flops: 95.6 MHz on option 0, top five paths all ending in `ras*`), so enable data writes from the imem pre-decode alone (write the free slot above the top; an unaccepted call-shaped word can then clobber the oldest entry, a hint-only cost that left cycles unchanged) and gate only the pointer / valid bits with the accept — and even then the same cone into the PC clock-enable and the widened FIFO `ix1` enables led option 0 at 14.8 ns.

title: MUL as a load-like EX->MEM op: product leaves the EX result mux, no EX bubble; exact load-use; AUIPC off the forward muxes
motivation:
Champion: 286.61 = 116.1 MHz x 4,051,640 CoreMark cycles. r5s0 found that
once control cones are cleaned up, the muldiv DSP product -> EX result
AND-OR -> EX/MEM.alu_result path is the top path on all three place
options, tied with forward mux -> adder -> alu_result. Two attempts to
re-shape that mux in place lost ~5% each; registering the product was
left untried because it was priced at +2.3% cycles.

Measured for this hypothesis (Verilator cosim prototype on the champion
RTL, CRCs valid): a MUL that never bubbles EX and instead behaves like a
LOAD (one "use" bubble only for a consumer directly behind it), together
with a load-use detector that ignores rs1/rs2 fields the ID instruction
does not read, gives 4,038,316 cycles = -13,324 cycles = +0.33%
iter/cycle. That removes ~60k raw EX bubbles but saves only ~13k cycles:
the core is imem-bound (0.78 words/cycle), the fetch FIFO banks a word
during almost every backend bubble, so a backend bubble costs only ~22%
of its raw count. Consequences: (a) backend IPC micro-opts are worth
well under 1% each and cannot clear the bar alone; (b) the same discount
makes backend bubbles cheap to SPEND, so the M path can be given a whole
extra stage of slack at essentially zero cycle cost.

NOT measured: Fmax. No Gowin run fitted in the generation budget, so the
Fmax half below is path arithmetic only. The honest expectation is below
the 4.6% acceptance bar unless the median place option follows.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU become a two-stage op that spans EX -> MEM, like
   a LOAD. EX only captures the forwarded, 33-bit sign/zero-extended
   operands into ma_q/mb_q on the edge the MUL leaves EX (enable =
   !stall_ex_mem, not squashed). The 33x33 product is computed during MEM
   from those flops and merged in the mux that already sits in front of
   MEM/WB.alu_result (load_data / product / EX result, one-hot selects
   from EX/MEM ctrl flops). A MUL never raises ex_busy. A MUL in MEM is
   never a memory op, so no dmem stall can hold it and ma_q/mb_q need no
   hold beyond the EX/MEM enable.
2. Hazard: the existing load-use detector fires for
   id_ex.mem_read || id_ex.is_mul, so a consumer directly behind a MUL
   takes the ordinary one-cycle bubble and then forwards from MEM/WB
   (select 10), exactly as after a LOAD. The registered forwarding
   selects stay valid: stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb
   keep their meaning, so ID/EX still captures exactly when EX/MEM and
   MEM/WB advance. Nothing ever selects EX/MEM.alu_result (01) of a MUL.
3. The EX result mux loses the M term for MUL. DIV/REM keep the stalling
   muldiv unit (0 divides in CoreMark); its result is also taken through
   the pre-MEM/WB mux via a small result register if that is needed to
   remove `m_op & m_result` from ex_other entirely, leaving
   ex_other = link (pc+4) only.
4. Exact load-use: qualify the rs1 compare with "opcode is not
   LUI/AUIPC/JAL" and the rs2 compare with "opcode is OP/STORE/BRANCH"
   (3 opcode bits each, from the same IF/ID word the detector already
   reads). Included in the measured +0.33%.
5. AUIPC result = the existing flop-launched `in.pc + in.imm` adder
   (branch_target), ORed into ex_other. alu_a is then always forwarded
   rs1, so the separate alu_a 3:1 mux and fwd_a/op_a registers are
   deleted and EX/MEM.alu_result / MEM/WB.alu_result each lose one of
   their four 32-bit forward-mux loads.
6. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the MUL stand-in formulas are evaluated in
   MEM from the same operand flops (32-bit a_q/b_q), DIV stand-ins keep
   the 2-cycle handshake; real and ALTOPS branches stay consistent.

Why it should help: the product path becomes DSP -> hi/lo select ->
write-back mux -> MEM/WB.alu_result (two mux levels fewer than today,
and off the forwarded EX cone), the EX result AND-OR shrinks by one
32-bit term, forward sources lose fan-out, and iter/cycle rises 0.33%.
If the MEM-stage product is still near the top of the median option, set
a registered product (MUL takes one more use-bubble): by the measured
discount that costs roughly 0.5% cycles, not 2.3%.

Guard rails from LESSONS: do not hand-force the EX result AND-OR mapping
(no syn_keep, no explicit priority mux); read the worst paths from the
median option of `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`, not
option 0; required cycle count after the change is <= 4,038,316.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-001-r6s0 (regression, -1.89%): Turning MUL into a load-like EX->MEM op delivered exactly its measured cycle half and none of its unmeasured Fmax half — 281.19 = 113.56 MHz median (106.0/113.6/113.6) x 4,038,440 CoreMark cycles (measured, +0.33% iter/cycle; Fmax 116.12 -> 113.56, -2.2%; LUT4 2788 -> 2702, FF 764 -> 800; formal 53/53 and cosim clean first try) — because on this device the 33x33 DSP product is essentially a full-period path by itself, so moving it to another stage only moves the wall: with the forwarded operands captured every cycle in `ma_q/mb_q`, no `ex_busy` for MUL, the load-use detector widened to `mem_read | is_mul | is_div` and the product ORed in front of MEM/WB.alu_result, the M term really is gone from the EX result AND-OR, yet `mb_q` -> DSP -> hi/lo select -> MEM/WB.alu_result now leads the median option at 14.10 ns with only 5 cells (DSP delay plus route to and from the DSP column, not LUT depth, so "two mux levels fewer" bought nothing), tied within 0.006 ns with EX/MEM.alu_result and MEM/WB.alu_result -> forward mux -> adder -> EX/MEM.alu_result (9 cells each, no faster for having lost the M term, the `alu_a` 3:1 mux and a forward-source load), ID/EX.pc -> pc+imm / pc+4 -> `ex_other` -> EX/MEM.alu_result (9 cells, the path item 5's AUIPC-through-`branch_target` creates) and dmem BSRAM -> load extract -> MEM/WB.alu_result (8 cells, now sharing its endpoint mux with the product) — the third slot after r5s0 and r5s2 in which taking one family out of the tied ~8.8 ns wall moved the median by zero or less, with a loss that sits inside the +/-3.5% equivalent-RTL placement spread and so cannot be attributed, and Fmax was once more "path arithmetic only" at hypothesis time; what else it measured: (a) exact load-use (rs1/rs2 compares qualified by `uses_rs1 = !(instr[2] & (instr[3] | instr[4]))`, `uses_rs2 = instr[5] & !instr[2]`) was built, timed and removed — worth 124 cycles (4,038,316 vs 4,038,440, +0.003%) for -3.9% Fmax (109.17 median, 101.9/109.2/109.2, top path `imem_ready` -> IF/ID instr -> hazard compare -> `stall_if` -> `v0` / PC: any gate added to the load-use compare sits on the latest signal of the fetch-accept cone), and it also needs an RVFI-only shadow regfile because cosim compares `rs1_rdata`/`rs2_rdata` with regs[field] even for fields an instruction does not read (formal `reg` check 308 s vs ~55 s) — do not re-propose it; (b) the same MUL change with `op_a`/`fwd_a` restored timed 110.47 (105.5/110.5/110.5) with the divider on top — `quo_q` -> sign fix-up negate -> MEM/WB.alu_result (10 cells) and `fwd_rs1` -> |a| negate -> `quo_q` — so a DIV result merged in MEM wants r5s0's registered divider pre/post steps underneath it (implementer's untested follow-up, 0 CoreMark cost), and "AUIPC off the forward muxes = +2.8%" is one placement sample each way, not a result; (c) ~60k raw EX bubbles removed (94k MUL bubbles out, 34.5k MUL-use bubbles in) saved 13.2k cycles, i.e. a backend bubble cost ~22% of a cycle on the imem-bound r4s2 champion, confirming that no backend IPC micro-opt was worth 1% there — but sibling r6s2 merged this round (315.15 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 cycles, BSRAM next-word replay lifting the 0.78 words/cycle fetch ceiling), so that discount and every backend count in r5s0's lesson are stale: re-count on the new champion before sizing or dismissing MUL-as-load, load-use or dmem-stall ideas (scribe's inference, untested: with fetch no longer starved a backend bubble costs closer to a full cycle, which would make this verified, UNMERGED change — it touches no if_stage.sv, only core.sv wiring overlaps r6s2 — worth more than +0.33% there, and "bubbles are cheap to spend" on a registered product correspondingly less true); hence: do not re-propose moving the multiply between stages as an Fmax idea — the only cut that shortens the product path is a register inside the multiply (the unimplemented `MUL_PIPE` fallback, which needs a second hazard term for a consumer two behind the MUL), it pays only if the forward mux -> adder families move in the same change, and before trying it check DSP register packing in the synthesis report, since this build's path launches from the fabric flop `mb_q_9` where the champion's launched from the DSP cell `prod_*` (r5s0; whether operand-register packing was lost was not checked); gotchas if the structure is reused: mem_stage ORs `m_result` into the write-back mux, which is correct only while an M op leaves EX with EX/MEM.alu_result == 0 (`sel_add` = 0 and nothing in `ex_other`), a use-bubble for a consumer behind a DIV must be gated with `!ex_busy` in `flush_id` or the still-running DIV is flushed out of ID/EX, and the operand flops need no enable because a MUL in MEM is never a memory op and so is never held by a dmem stall.

title: Path-validated BSRAM fetch-backup store read 2 fetches ahead from PC flops (covers imem stalls, off the PC loop)
motivation:
The champion (286.61 = 116.1 MHz x 4,051,640 cycles) is walled on both axes
for small edits: Fmax is a tie of true datapath families (r5s0/r5s2: deleting
some of them measured ~0) and every counted IPC item except one is < 2.5%.
The exception is fetch starvation: 541k of 4.05M cycles have decode idle
because imem delivers only 0.78 words/cycle. r5s1 proved that a second, in-core
instruction source removes most of it (+12.4% iter/cycle with 256 entries,
+14.6% with 1024, CoreMark validated) and lost only on Fmax (71.7 MHz) because
its 44-bit ASYNC LUT-RAM was read inside the single-cycle PC loop: pc[9:2]
fan-out 664, a 5.2 ns address net, 2000 LUT4 of read muxes, tag compare ->
fetch_acc -> PC enable, third pc+imm adder. Its lesson asks for exactly one
thing: a form whose store read is OUT of the PC cycle. This hypothesis is
that form. Break-even is ~108 MHz (-6.6% Fmax) at +12% iter/cycle.
NOT measured at hypothesis time (20-minute slot): neither cycles nor Fmax of
this form; the cycle estimate is derived from r5s1's FIFO-entry prototype and
the r5s0 event counts, the Fmax estimate is path reasoning only.

some of them measured ~0) and every counted IPC item except one is < 2.5%.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a 1024-entry SYNCHRONOUS (BSRAM, ~3 x 18Kbit, 0 LUT read muxes) backup
store to if_stage that supplies the fetch word on cycles where imem is not
ready. Nothing of the store is read, compared or enabled inside the PC cycle:
it is addressed by the PC FLOPS, read every cycle (no CE), and its output is
registered once before use, so all the fetch loop sees is a few flop bits
ANDed into one new LUT input.

Key trick (what makes a 2-cycle-old read usable): the entry indexed by fetch
address Y does not hold the word at Y, it holds the word that was fetched TWO
accepted fetches after Y, plus the two steer bits (s1,s2: 1 = "PC was steered
by a folded JAL / predicted-taken branch", 0 = "pc+4") of the two transitions
in between: F[Y] = {v, tag=Y[19:12], s1, s2, word}. A steer target is a pure
function of (pc, instr), so same start address + same two steer decisions +
no redirect in between => same address => the stored word is the word at the
current PC. Validation needs NO address compare against the live PC and no
next-PC value, only bit compares against flops.

Read side (fetch sequence X0 -> X1 -> X2; adv_q = registered "PC changed at
the last edge"; a1_q / a1_v_q = steer bit of the last PC transition / "it was
a fetch advance, not a redirect" - 2 flops, the only new state updated with
the accept; a2_q / a2_v_q = the transition before):
 - BSRAM read address = pc[11:2] flop outputs, every cycle. ptag_q <=
   {pc[31:20]==0, pc[19:12]} also every cycle (no enable). So in the first
   cycle at X1 (adv_q=1) the RAM output is F[X0] and ptag_q is X0's tag.
 - End of that cycle, enable = adv_q (a FLOP, never fetch_acc - r5s2's CE
   gotcha): nx_word_q <= F.word; nx_s2_q <= F.s2;
   nx_ok1_q <= F.v && F.tag == ptag_q && F.s1 == a1_q && a1_v_q && !collide.
   Path: BSRAM clk-to-out -> 9-bit compare -> flop D, nothing late in it.
   nx_* then holds until the end of the first cycle at X2.
 - First cycle at X2: bk_ok = adv_q && nx_ok1_q && a1_v_q && (nx_s2_q ==
   a1_q) (a1 now describes X1->X2): one LUT of flops.
   fetch_acc = (imem_ready || bk_ok) && !redirect && (!v1 || !stall): the
   final LUT keeps 4 inputs and `stall` keeps its depth. Backup only in the
   first cycle at a PC is enough: a PC is only held with a valid backup when
   the FIFO is full.
 - Word: live = imem_ready ? imem_data : nx_word_q feeds ONLY the FIFO data
   flops and the JAL/branch pre-decode. A backup word is ALWAYS pushed into
   the 2-entry FIFO (push = fetch_acc && (v0 || stall || !imem_ready)),
   never bypassed to decode, so out.instr / NOP mux / decoder / load-use /
   stall are identical to the champion. Cost: one bubble the first time the
   FIFO is empty on an imem stall; after that the FIFO runs at occupancy
   >= 1 and later imem stalls are hidden (same word-enters-through-the-FIFO
   form as r5s1's timing-safe prototype).
 - Steering of a backup word: steer = pht_rd[1] ? T1 : T0 with
   T1 = imem_ready ? (jal_l | br_l) : (jal_b | br_b), T0 = imem_ready ?
   jal_l : jal_b; the backup pre-decode bits come from flops and merge in
   the existing second pre-decode LUT level, in parallel with the PHT
   RAM16 + 16:1 read, so the tied pc -> PHT -> steer -> PC loop keeps its
   depth. The single pc+fimm adder is kept: its immediate input becomes
   imem_ready ? fimm(imem_data) : fimm(nx_word_q) (pre-selected J/B in a
   registered nx_fimm_q if needed; LUT3 -> LUT5 in front of the adder, no
   third carry chain, no post-adder mux, PC D mux unchanged).
   pred_taken / pred_ctr ride with the word exactly as today.
Write side (flop-launched, one cycle late): wr_word_q <= imem_data every
cycle; wr_en_q <= imem_ready && fetch_acc && a1_v_q && a2_v_q && window;
index/tag = fetch address two accepts back, kept WITHOUT accept-enabled data
flops: ppc_q <= pc every cycle, h1_q <= ppc_q and h2_q <= h1_q on adv_q,
X0 = adv_q ? h1_q : h2_q; stored s1 = a2_q, s2 = a1_q. Entries are written
atomically, so a stale read is a tag miss or the same word; a read whose
index equals the index written at the same edge sets `collide` (registered
10-bit compare) so nothing depends on BSRAM read-during-write mode. After a
redirect two words are unbacked (58k redirects x ~0.3 bubble each).
The array is `initial`-zeroed (v=0), no reset loop; FENCE / FENCE.I leaving
EX starts a 1024-cycle invalidation sweep on the write port with bk_ok
forced 0 (r5s1's rs_clear rule). stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem /
hold_mem_wb, ID, EX, MEM and RVFI are untouched, so r2s0's forwarding-select
invariant holds. Formal does not constrain imem contents, so a replayed word
is just another fetched word to riscv-formal; if a 1024 x 44 memory makes
the BMC slow, expose DEPTH as a parameter of the same RTL (smaller depth =
more aliasing inside the BMC window, no formal/ file touched).

Expected: iter/cycle +10..13% (4.05M -> ~3.60-3.68M cycles), Fmax -0..5%
from ~150 new flops and 3 BSRAMs beside the fetch stage -> fitness +5..12%.

Implementation order (measure each step): (1) cosim CoreMark cycles first
(`python3 -m tools.eval.cosim . bench`); expect <= 3.68M with CRCs
unchanged - if above ~3.75M stop, the idea cannot clear 4.6%. (2)
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`; check the store inferred
as BSRAM (count +3, no new RAM16/flop array) and read the MEDIAN option's
top paths. Fallbacks by symptom: pc flops -> BSRAM address route on top ->
dedicated replicated 10-bit index register loaded from the PC D value, or
512 x 36; nx_word_q -> pre-decode -> steer on top -> store jal/br bits and
the J/B-selected immediate in the entry (72-bit budget); BSRAM out -> tag
compare -> nx_ok1_q on top -> enable the BSRAM output register and delay
ptag_q/a1 by one stage (3-fetch-ahead, s1..s3); cycles short -> add a
second holding rank (bk_q, enable adv_q) so the backup survives a FIFO-full
hold. Do not add any select derived from the store to out.instr, the PC D
mux or the FIFO valids.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-002-r6s1 (regression, +7.00%): The path-validated fetch-backup store worked and beat the r4s2 champion — 306.66 = 110.64 MHz median (101.1/110.6/110.6) x 3,607,862 CoreMark cycles (measured, CRCs valid; +12.3% iter/cycle vs 4,051,640, the good end of its 3.60-3.68M estimate; LUT4 2788 -> 2919, FF 764 -> 953, BSRAM 4 -> 7 all SDPB, LUT-RAM unchanged at 48; formal 53/53 and cosim clean first try) — and is a "regression" only because sibling r6s2 (untagged 4096-entry sequential next-word BSRAM predictor, non-steering words only) won the same round with 315.15 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 cycles: the whole extra machinery here (8-bit tag, two steer bits validating a word read 2 fetches ahead, replay of steering words and steer targets with `imem_ready`-selected pre-decode/`fimm` in front of the single pc+imm adder, ~190 new flops) bought just 74.9k cycles (+2.1% iter/cycle) over the simple form and gave back 4.7% Fmax, so the lesson is that once the store read is out of the PC cycle (synchronous BSRAM addressed by the pc flops every cycle, output re-registered with a flop enable, word entering ONLY through the fetch FIFO — r5s1's prescription, now confirmed twice: no store, tag-compare, `nx_*` or write-port path is in the top 5 of any place option) the fetch-starvation prize is ~10% for the plainest table and coverage refinements are worth ~2%, less than one placement's noise; the Fmax loss itself is NOT attributed — it shows up as the champion's own EX/forwarding paths closing ~0.4 ns worse (implementer's unmeasured candidates: ~110 extra loads on `imem_ready` from the word/immediate/pre-decode selects and placement pull of 3 BSRAMs on the pc flops), and option 0 moved 114.3 -> 101.1 MHz between two builds whose netlists differ by 7 LUTs (r6s2 likewise ranged 103.9-116.1 over four builds), so the 2.7% gap between the two slots is inside build-to-build spread and a single `--all-options` median cannot rank ideas that are < ~5% apart. Carry-overs: (a) the only store-related path that ever led was self-inflicted — `wr_en_q <= imem_ready && fetch_acc && ...` put `imem_ready` -> decode -> load-use -> `stall` -> `fetch_acc` -> `wr_en_q` on top of every option (108.5 MHz median) and dropping the qualifier gave 110.64 with an identical cycle count, because the entry is true whenever imem delivers at the current PC — so make table writes idempotent and never put `fetch_acc`/`stall` into the D or CE of a new flop (r5s2's CE gotcha applies to write enables too); (b) `initial` zero-fill alone is not enough for any instruction-caching table — the cocotb tests reset and load a different image in one simulation, so both r6 slots needed a post-reset invalidation sweep on the write port; (c) riscv-formal gives ZERO coverage of stall-hiding fetch logic (`formal/wrapper_si.sv` ties `io_imemReady` to 1 and the sweep outlasts the BMC window), so 53/53 says nothing about replay and correctness rests on stalled cosim vs the ISS plus a dedicated cocotb test; (d) on the new r6s2 champion the residual of this idea (steer targets + steering words, 3,682,766 -> ~3,607,862) is at most ~+2.1%, under the 4.6% acceptance bar, so do not re-propose it standalone — only as an add-on shown Fmax-neutral over several builds.

title: Sequential next-word predictor in BSRAM: untagged, read one cycle ahead from the pc flops, replayed through the fetch FIFO only
motivation:
Direction / target prediction is spent on this champion: 58k redirects
are 2.9% of cycles in total, the RAS measured +0.8%, gshare is no better
than bimodal. The one large iter/cycle prize left is the 541k
fetch-starved cycles (13.4% of 4.05M) - imem delivers 0.78 words/cycle.
r5s1 proved that predicting the imem word from a PC-indexed table is
worth +12.4% iter/cycle (formal + cosim clean) and lost only on Fmax
(71.7 MHz): its 44-bit ASYNC LUT-RAM table with tags was read inside the
PC cycle (pc fan-out 664, 5.2 ns address net, tag compare and a third
pc+imm adder in the PC loop). Its lesson asks for a form whose read is
OUT of the PC cycle. This is that form, with no tag, no adder, no clock
enable and no PHT/decode-cone involvement.
Facts checked at hypothesis time: all hot CoreMark code lies in
0x001c..0x30e0 (text+rodata 16.7 KB, memset at 0x39c4), so a 16 KB
exact-address window covers it; the timed netlist drives io_imemData
from LFSR flops (fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so today's fetch cones launch
from plain flops; Fmax of this design was NOT measured (no time for a
Gowin run) - the implementer must run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` on the first working build and iterate.

hypothesis.motivation:
Direction / target prediction is spent on this champion: 58k redirects
are 2.9% of cycles in total, the RAS measured +0.8%, gshare is no better
than bimodal. The one large iter/cycle prize left is the 541k
fetch-starved cycles (13.4% of 4.05M) - imem delivers 0.78 words/cycle.
r5s1 proved that predicting the imem word from a PC-indexed table is
worth +12.4% iter/cycle (formal + cosim clean) and lost only on Fmax
(71.7 MHz): its 44-bit ASYNC LUT-RAM table with tags was read inside the
PC cycle (pc fan-out 664, 5.2 ns address net, tag compare and a third
pc+imm adder in the PC loop). Its lesson asks for a form whose read is
OUT of the PC cycle. This is that form, with no tag, no adder, no clock
enable and no PHT/decode-cone involvement.
Facts checked at hypothesis time: all hot CoreMark code lies in
0x001c..0x30e0 (text+rodata 16.7 KB, memset at 0x39c4), so a 16 KB
exact-address window covers it; the timed netlist drives io_imemData
from LFSR flops (fpga/core_bench_si.sv), so today's fetch cones launch
from plain flops; Fmax of this design was NOT measured (no time for a
Gowin run) - the implementer must run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` on the first working build and iterate.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a "next-word predictor" to if_stage: a synchronous-read BSRAM table
that predicts the instruction word at pc+4 one cycle before it is used.

Table: direct-mapped, UNTAGGED, exact address map of the window
pc[31:14]==0: 4096 x 31 bit {valid, instr[31:2]} (8 BSRAM as 4096x4;
device has 46, core uses 4). Each index maps to exactly one address, so
there is no tag, no aliasing and no invalidation; code outside the
window never hits. `syn_ramstyle = "block_ram"`, `initial` zero-fill
(valid=0), no reset loop. Parameterise the index width and shrink it
under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL` (e.g. 4 bits) so BMC does not carry a 127
kbit memory.

Read (every cycle, NO clock enable, address pins fed by flops only):
entry i holds the word at address 4*(i+1), read address = pc[13:2].
At cycle M the registered BSRAM output is word(pc[M-1]+4), which is the
word at the current pc iff the previous cycle was a sequential accept:
  seq_q  <= fetch_acc && !steer_eff          (one flop, reset 0)
  rs_hit  = seq_q && out.valid && (pc[31:14]==0) && !coll_q && !rs_off
i.e. ONE LUT level behind the BSRAM output (window detect runs in
parallel with the 2.3 ns BSRAM clock-to-out). If the implementer finds
the write-side -1 awkward, the equivalent is entry i = word at 4*i with
read address pc[13:2]+1.

Only NON-steering words are stored (imem_data[1:0]==11, not an aligned
JAL, not a br_ok branch). A hit therefore always means pc <= pc+4: no
third adder, no immediate mux, no stored pre-decode, PHT loop unchanged
except `steer_eff = imem_ready && steer` (same LUT).

Use:
  fetch_acc = (imem_ready || rs_hit) && !redirect && (!v1 || !stall)
  word      = imem_ready ? imem_data : {rs_out.instr, 2'b11}
  push      = fetch_acc && (v0 || stall || !imem_ready)
The replayed word NEVER enters the decode bypass (out.instr / out.valid
keep `imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP`): it is written into the FIFO data
flops only (pt=0), so BSRAM clock-to-out ends in FIFO flops and the PC /
v0 / v1 enables, not in decoder -> ID/EX.op_b (a tied family). A
stalled-imem cycle with an empty FIFO is still a bubble, but the hit
refills one word of slack; in steady state bubbles = 0.22 * (1 - h) per
fetch (r5s1's timing-safe prototype kept its full +12.4% this way).

Write (registered, flop-launched, no stall/fetch_acc/redirect term):
  w_en_q   <= imem_ready && pc[31:14]==0 && pc[13:2]!=0 && storable
  w_idx_q  <= pc[13:2] - 1 ;  w_data_q <= {1'b1, imem_data[31:2]}
(imem_data is the true content of pc whenever imem_ready, also on a
wrong path). coll_q <= w_en_q && (w_idx_q == pc[13:2]) kills a hit read
in a same-address write cycle. rs_off is a sticky flop set by a
FENCE/FENCE.I leaving EX or by any store with an address inside the
window (self-modifying code), cleared only by reset.

Nothing else changes: stall_id / flush_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb,
redirect handling (redir_q clears v0/v1, loads PC; seq_q is 0 after it
because fetch_acc is 0), PHT, EX. A word after a steer or redirect is
never replayed (accepted cost).

ISS trace of coremark.elf (test/cosim/reference.py, hypothesis time):
2.02M executed words are non-steering AND reached sequentially (about
0.65 of the ~3.1M-instruction run; the denominator is inferred because
the ISS spun in the exit loop), 0.34M more are non-steering steer
targets, 0 are outside the 16 KB window. Not an RTL cycle count.
Expected: stalled fetches whose word is non-steering and reached
sequentially, h ~ 0.6-0.7 -> ~330-380k of the 541k starved cycles
removed -> +8..10% iter/cycle. Break-even needs Fmax within about -4%
of 116.1 MHz. New paths to watch in the --all-options report:
(1) BSRAM out -> rs_hit -> fetch_acc -> PC CE / v0,v1 / seq_q;
(2) BSRAM out -> word mux -> FIFO data D;
(3) pc flops -> 8 BSRAM address pins (pure route; if the placer drags
    the pc flops, use a dedicated syn_keep'ed copy of pc[13:2]).
Fallbacks if (1) leads: 2048 entries (hot code would need a 13-bit
window check, so prefer keeping 4096), or register `out.valid && window`
is impossible (same-cycle data), so instead drop rs_hit from the PC
data path by keeping PC's D mux independent of it (it already is; only
the CE sees it). Optional second step only if timing has slack: a
second copy read at pc+fimm[13:2] to also cover steer targets (+~0.1 h).

Export a registered pulse when a valid MISC-MEM (FENCE/FENCE.I) instruction leaves EX (flop only, no new logic on EX cones).

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-003-r6s2 (improvement, +9.96%): The whole gain is iterations/cycle and none of it was paid back in Fmax — scored 315.15 = 116.06 MHz median (107.6/116.1/116.1, the r4s2 champion's own per-option profile to within 0.06 MHz) x 3,682,766 CoreMark cycles (measured, CRCs valid; 4,051,640 -> 3,682,766, +10.0% iter/cycle, 369k of the 541k fetch-starved cycles removed; LUT4 2788 -> 2944, FF 764 -> 849, BSRAM 4 -> 12 of 46, LUT-RAM 48; formal 53/53 first try, cosim clean) against a +6% forecast that had budgeted ~4% of Fmax loss — because the table was cut down until its read adds nothing to the single-cycle PC loop, paying in BSRAM bits instead of logic: an UNTAGGED exact-address map (4096 x 31b `{valid, instr[31:2]}` over `pc[31:14]==0`; all hot CoreMark code sits below 16 KB, so depth replaces r5s1's tag compare and any aliasing logic), a synchronous BSRAM read every cycle with no clock enable and flop-driven address pins, only NON-steering words stored (a hit always means `pc <= pc+4`: no third adder, no stored pre-decode, PHT loop unchanged apart from `steer_eff = imem_ready && steer`), the replayed word written only into the fetch-FIFO data flops and never into the decode bypass, a registered write with no `stall`/`fetch_acc` term, and every hit qualifier (sequential accept, window, same-index write collision, `rs_off`/`rs_kill`, sweep busy) computed one cycle early into ONE flop so that `rs_hit = hit_q && rs_out.valid` is the only new term in `fetch_acc`; the cycle gain was forecast from an ISS trace alone (2.02M of ~3.1M executed words are non-steering and reached sequentially -> 330-380k cycles) and landed at 369k, so for fetch-side ideas a trace count of eligible words times the measured starvation rate is a good enough IPC estimate without an RTL prototype. The Fmax half is NOT attributed and was not there on the first build: four builds, one per variant, gave medians of 108.9 (plan as written), 103.9 (+ post-reset sweep: a 13-bit counter and a mux on the registered write index), 107.8 (+ `pc_ra`, a `syn_preserve` copy of `pc[13:2]` with the same next-state that feeds only the 8 BSRAM read-address pins) and 116.06 (+ the `hit_q` fold, which the implementer credits), yet in every report that was printed the top paths were the champion's own families (EX/MEM.alu_result -> forward select -> ID/EX.fwd_*, `alu_op` -> alu_result, `imem_ready` -> decoder -> ID/EX, `pc` -> PHT -> PC) closing up to ~1 ns worse and never a BSRAM-output, `rs_hit` or write-port path — so a new BSRAM table costs Fmax here through placement, not through a cone, a -6..-10% first build of one is not a verdict, and the remedies to try are a dedicated preserved address register plus as few nets as possible between the RAM and the existing loop, while an off-path 13-bit counter moving the median 5 MHz means neither remedy is proven by a single build (`hit_q`'s D and the 12 `pc_ra` enables do hang on `fetch_acc` and the build still matched the champion, so r5s2/r6s1's "no `fetch_acc` in a new flop" rule did not bind for a dozen loads placed with the pc flops; only option 0's paths of the final build were printed — EX forward/ALU at 14.59 ns — so what limits the 116.06 median is unmeasured). Gotchas: Gowin synthesis rejects a single `initial` loop over 4096 entries (EX3934, 2000-iteration cap), so zero-fill with two nested loops; BSRAM contents survive reset and the cocotb suites reset and then run another program (4 failures on build 1), hence the invalidation sweep (4096 replay-free cycles after reset, over before CoreMark's start marker at cycle ~13.5k), which is compiled out under `RISCV_FORMAL`, and since `formal/wrapper_si.sv` ties `io_imemReady` to 1 the 53/53 never exercises a replay — correctness rests on stalled cosim vs the ISS and `test/test_fetch_replay.py`; replay assumes imem content is stable (a store into the window or a FENCE sets sticky `rs_off` until reset) and code outside the 16 KB window never hits, so the gain is tied to this benchmark layout. What is left (scribe's arithmetic): at most ~172k starved cycles (4.7%), of which r6s1 showed ~75k (+2.1%) reachable by also replaying steering words and steer targets at an Fmax cost, so fetch starvation is no longer a standalone lever above the 4.6% bar.

title: Backend bubble removal: stores stop stalling the pipeline on dmem-not-ready (bus registers hold, pipeline advances) + MUL as load-like EX->MEM op
motivation:
After r6s2 the fetch side is no longer starved (3,682,766 cycles for 2,922,015
instructions; lost cycles are now ~192k dmem-stall, ~195k load-use, ~94k MUL
bubbles, ~116k redirect slots, <=172k fetch). r6s0 measured a backend bubble at
only ~22% of a cycle on the imem-bound r4s2 champion; with the replay store in
place it is close to a full cycle, so backend bubbles are the remaining
iter/cycle lever. Two of them can be removed WITHOUT touching the tied EX
forward-mux -> adder/compare cone or the fetch cone (champion option-0 top
paths re-timed at hypothesis time: alu_result -> jalr_sum[1] -> ex_w_en ->
ID/EX.fwd_*, alu_op/fwd_a -> alu_result, imem_ready -> load-use -> pc_ra, all
14.54-14.59 ns): a STORE never needs the bus answer, and a MUL result is only
needed one stage later. The whole dmem_stall freeze for a store whose bus
cycle is not ready (22% of stores) is pure waste whenever the instruction
behind it is not a memory op.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) Deferred store, no buffer and NO mux on the bus. Give EX/MEM a dedicated
set of "bus registers" loaded in EX: mem_addr (already there), bus_wdata
(byte/half replicated from forwarded rs2 in EX), bus_wen[3:0] and bus_ren
(byte mask + misalign gating from jalr_sum[1:0] and mem_width in EX, 0 for
bubbles / ex_busy / redir_q squash). io_dmemAddr/WData/WEn/REn are these
flops directly (the dmem BSRAM still absorbs the address flop; do NOT put a
pending-store mux in front of io_dmemAddr - core_bench reads dmem
asynchronously and Gowin only infers BSRAM by absorbing a plain address
flop). Their clock enable is !bus_busy, bus_busy = !dmem_ready &&
(bus_ren | |bus_wen). The rest of the pipeline freezes (today's dmem_stall:
stall_id / stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb, unchanged semantics so the registered
forwarding selects stay valid) only when
   dmem_stall = bus_busy && (bus_ren || ((id_ex.mem_read | id_ex.mem_write) && !redir_q))
i.e. a not-yet-accepted LOAD freezes as before, but a not-yet-accepted STORE
lets its instruction retire and non-memory instructions flow through MEM
while the bus registers simply hold the write until io_dmemReady; the freeze
comes back only when the instruction in EX itself needs the bus (so memory
order is preserved with no address compare and no forwarding). All terms are
flops (dmem_ready is a flop in the stall generator), same depth as today's
dmem_stall. The !redir_q term is required: the redirect cycle must never be
held (redir_q <= mispredict && !stall assumes it). A store only enters MEM
on an edge where the bus registers load it, so RVFI mem_* fields (still from
the pipeline payload) and rs_kill stay in sync. Misaligned ops (wen=ren=0)
stop stalling too. Gotchas: a deferred write lands up to a few cycles after
its instruction retires, so check the harness end condition (EBREAK right
after a UART/marker store) still sees the write, and note riscv-formal ties
the bus ready inputs, so correctness rests on stalled cosim + the cocotb
test below. Size it first with a cosim counter: stores whose bus
cycle is not ready and whose follower in EX is not a mem op (estimate 35-50k
cycles, +1.0..1.4%).
(2) Re-apply r6s0's verified, unmerged MUL-as-load change on this champion
(operands captured every cycle in ma_q/mb_q, no ex_busy for MUL, product
ORed in front of MEM/WB.alu_result, load-use detector widened to
mem_read | is_mul, DIV unchanged in EX): removes ~60k raw EX bubbles, which
now cost ~a full cycle each (+1.2..1.6%) instead of the +0.33% measured on
the fetch-starved champion. Keep r6s0's gotchas (M op leaves EX with
alu_result == 0; use-bubble gated with !ex_busy; no exact load-use).
Build and score (1) alone first with `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options`; add (2) only if the median stays within ~1.5% of (1)'s.
Expected: ~3.58M cycles (+2.5..3% iter/cycle) at neutral Fmax; this is an
honest sub-5% estimate, the upside needs a favourable placement.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-001-r7s0 (regression, +2.39%): Both backend-bubble removals worked first try at neutral Fmax and still could not merge, because the whole prize is smaller than the 4.6% acceptance margin — 322.68 = 116.39 MHz median (101.8/116.4/116.4 vs the champion's 107.6/116.1/116.1) x 3,607,115 CoreMark cycles (measured, CRCs valid; 75,651 cycles saved, +2.10% iter/cycle vs 3,682,766; LUT4 2944 -> 2896, FF 849 -> 858, 12 BSRAM and 2 DSP still inferred; formal 53/53 first try, cosim 5/5) is the highest score measured on this core and a "regression" only because acceptance needed 329.7 — so a correct iter/cycle micro-opt whose own forecast is under the bar (this one said "+3%, honest sub-5%") is a spent slot when proposed alone: stack such items, and since this diff is verified and unmerged the next backend hypothesis should start from it and add about as much again in the same build (~76k more cycles at this Fmax; scribe's arithmetic). What it established: (a) a not-ready STORE need not freeze the pipeline — dedicated EX/MEM bus flops (`mem_addr`, `bus_wdata`, `bus_wen`, `bus_ren`, pre-ORed `bus_act`; byte mask, misalign gating and replication computed in EX from `jalr_sum[1:0]`) with their own enable `!bus_hold`, `bus_busy = !dmem_ready && bus_act` and `dmem_stall = bus_busy && (bus_ren || (id_ex.bus_sync && !redirect))` keep memory order with no store buffer, no address compare and no mux in front of `io_dmemAddr`, and no bus-register or stall path is in the top 5 of the two median options (`imem_ready` lfsr -> hazard -> ID -> PC tied at 13.886 ns with `fwd_b` -> EX/MEM.alu_result; only outlier option 0 lists EX/MEM.alu_result -> dmem BSRAM pins, 15.11 ns, 6 cells, inside 0.01 ns of the usual forward/ALU families and not checked against the champion); (b) MUL-as-load (operands captured with `mul_en = !stall`, product ORed in front of MEM/WB.alu_result, load-use widened to `mem_read | is_mul`), which measured -2.2% Fmax on r4s2 in r6s0, cost nothing here and no `mb_q` -> DSP path is in any option's top 5, consistent with r6s0's reading that its loss was placement and not the product path; (c) the 75.7k cycles are about three quarters of the ~103k forecast (35-50k not-ready stores with a non-memory follower + ~60k net MUL bubbles), so even on the replay-store champion a raw backend-bubble count overstates the saving by roughly a quarter — and that is all that can be said, because the implementer skipped both the store-only build and the sizing counter the hypothesis asked for, so the split between the two parts is unknown (scribe's inference from the total; a per-part cosim cycle count takes a minute and should be mandatory for two-part hypotheses); (d) placement noise once more: pre-ORing `mem_read | is_mul` into one extra ID/EX flop for the load-use detector dropped the median to 108.2 MHz (110.6/108.2/108.2, top path EX/MEM.alu_result -> branch compare -> `upd_taken_q`, a cone neither variant touches) and was reverted, while the shipped RTL gave 116.39 in both local runs and in the evaluator — identical RTL reproduces, a one-flop edit can move the median 7%, so no single build attributes an Fmax change of that size. Gotchas if reused: a deferred store retires before its write lands and the cosim harness stops on the cycle EBREAK retires, so `bus_sync` must be `mem_read | mem_write | opcode == SYSTEM` (one pre-decoded ID/EX flop) or the last write is lost; `!redirect` is needed because the redirect cycle must never be held; riscv-formal ties the dmem ready input, so 53/53 never exercises a deferral and correctness rests on stalled cosim plus `test/test_store_defer.py` (accepted bus writes == retired stores, in order, exactly once, under 6 stall models); `fpga/core_bench_si.sv` writes whenever WEn != 0 regardless of ready, so a held write merely repeats.

title: Data-side stall hiding: in-core BSRAM load shadow (read at the EX address, used only when dmem is not ready) plus deferred store acceptance
motivation:
Champion = 315.15 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 cycles for ~2.92M retired
instructions (nret=1, so IPC <= 1): ~760k overhead cycles. r6s2 took
most of the imem-stall cost away with an in-core BSRAM replay store and
proved the recipe costs no Fmax when the table is read from flops and
adds one term to the stall cone. The data side still pays the full ~22%
bus stall: every LOAD/STORE in MEM with io_dmemReady=0 freezes the whole
pipeline (dmem_stall), ~192k cycles counted in r5s0 = ~5.2% of today's
cycles, and since fetch is no longer starved these cycles are no longer
hidden behind imem stalls. It is the largest untouched bucket (load-use
195k cannot be removed without touching the EX loop; predictor, RAS,
MUL moves and control-cone cleanups all measured < 1%). Fmax is walled
by 4-5 tied datapath families that r5s0/r5s2/r6s0 could not move, so
the only lever above the 4.6% bar is iterations/cycle, bought with
BSRAM bits (12 of 46 used) rather than logic in the tied cones.
NOT measured at hypothesis time (20 min budget): load/store split of
the 192k stall cycles, shadow hit rate, Fmax. Estimate: ~686k mem ops
(192k / 0.28 expected stall cycles each), ~3/4 loads -> ~140k cycles
from loads + 25-45k from stores = 4.5-5% fewer cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Data-side twin of r6s2. Bus-facing outputs stay plain EX/MEM flops
(io_dmemAddr MUST remain a bare flop: the bench dmem is an async-read
array that Gowin maps to BSRAM only by absorbing that flop; never put a
mux on io_dmemAddr).
(1) Load shadow. Direct-mapped 4096-word copy of data RAM in four
9-bit-wide byte-lane BSRAMs (8 data bits + 1 spare bit per lane: lane0
spare = valid, lanes1-3 spare = 3-bit tag addr[16:14]; index
addr[13:2]; window addr[31:17]==1 = the whole 0x20000-0x2FFFF RAM, so
MMIO at 0x1000_0000 and flash are never shadowed). Synchronous read
every cycle at the EX-stage rs1+imm adder output (jalr_sum, the net
that already feeds EX/MEM.mem_addr; use a preserved dedicated copy of
the read address if placement needs it, as pc_ra did). In MEM:
hit = valid && tag==mem_addr[16:14] && window && first_mem_cycle &&
!write_collision, where window / collision / first-cycle are computed
from flops in parallel with the BSRAM clock-to-out, so hit is ~2 LUT
levels behind the RAM. New stall: dmem_stall = mem_op && !dmem_ready &&
!(mem_read && hit). The shadow word is used ONLY when io_dmemReady=0
(bus data otherwise), so zero-stall behaviour and riscv-formal (ready
tied to 1) are unchanged. Keep the load path flat: duplicate the byte
extract/sign-extend for the shadow word and merge it in the existing
write-back mux with flop selects {mem_to_reg, dmem_ready} (one LUT5
instead of LUT3), no 2:1 in front of the extractor. RVFI mem_rdata
reports the word actually used.
Writes (registered, in order, no stall/fetch_acc term in data or
enable beyond 'op completes'): a bus-delivered load in the window
allocates (4 lanes + tag + valid); a word store allocates; a sub-word
store updates its lanes only on a clean hit and otherwise invalidates
the entry (lane0 valid=0) - always safe. A read whose index equals a
write still in flight is a forced miss. Post-reset invalidation sweep
of lane0 (BSRAM survives reset; compiled out under RISCV_FORMAL), two
nested initial loops for zero-fill.
(2) Deferred store acceptance (drop if it costs Fmax or breaks the
end-of-test UART/marker writes): a STORE whose bus write is not yet
accepted no longer freezes the pipeline while the instruction in EX is
not a memory op; dedicated bus registers (addr/wdata/wen, clock-enable
only, D = the same EX values) keep driving the write and the global
freeze becomes sb_pending && !dmem_ready && ID/EX.mem_op (all flops, one
LUT level as today). The freeze stays GLOBAL (PC, ID/EX, EX/MEM hold,
MEM/WB valid cleared) so the registered forwarding selects' invariant
'ID/EX captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance' still holds.
Expected: -4.5..-5% cycles (+4.7..+5.3% iter/cycle) at flat Fmax; the
only new late signal is BSRAM -> hit -> dmem_stall, about as long as
the existing imem_ready -> load-use -> stall arm it ORs with. Run
--all-options before and after part (2); correctness rests on stalled
cosim vs the ISS (stale shadow data shows up as an rd_wdata mismatch).

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-002-r7s1 (regression, -15.41%): The data-side twin of r6s2 kept its iterations/cycle half and lost about five times that to Fmax — scored 266.60 = 94.8 MHz median (evaluator's figure; 116.06 -> 94.8, -18.3%) x ~3.556M CoreMark cycles (scribe's inference from fitness — the implementer measured neither cycles nor shadow hit rate; ~127k of the ~192k dmem-stall cycles gone, +3.6% iter/cycle vs 3,682,766, about 90% of the ~140k forecast for loads; LUT4 2944 -> 3080, FF 849 -> 930, BSRAM 12 -> 21 of 46; formal 53/53 first try, stalled cosim clean; part (2), deferred stores, not attempted) — and the only evidence on why points at the two places where the load shadow departs from the recipe that made r6s2 free: (a) its read address is not a flop but the combinational EX `jalr_sum[13:2]` (forward mux -> rs1+imm adder, i.e. the end of the tied EX family), now also routed to the address pins of 9 new fixed-site BSRAMs, with no preserved copy possible short of a second adder (implementer's note), and (b) its hit is not pre-folded into one flop: BSRAM clock-to-out -> `{valid, tag == mem_addr[16:14]}` -> `load_hit` -> `dmem_stall` -> every pipeline enable and the PC, which in the one report that was printed (option 0, 100.98 MHz vs the champion's 107.6 on that option) sits in a five-way tie within 0.03 ns (`u_mem/sh_meta` BSRAM -> `u_if/pc[31]`, 8 cells, 15.17 ns) with the usual forward/ALU and `imem_ready` -> decode families, themselves ~0.6 ns slower than on the champion; the two options that set the 94.8 median were never printed, so the split between the new cone and placement pull is unattributed, and this was the design's first and only build (a single option-0 `make timing` at the end of the 30-minute slot, no `--all-options`, no timing iteration), whereas r6s2 needed four builds to climb from 108.9 to 116.06. Two rules follow: an in-core BSRAM table is free here only when its address pins come from flops and its output reaches a stall/enable as one pre-qualified bit, so a table that must be read at the EX adder output is a different, unproven design and not "r6s2's recipe" — budget it as an Fmax risk and start the first Gowin `--all-options` run as soon as lint passes; and the load shadow alone tops out at ~+3.6% even at flat Fmax (~326 against the 329.7 bar; at these cycles break-even with the champion is ~112 MHz and acceptance needs ~117 MHz), so like r7s0 it cannot merge by itself and is only worth another slot stacked on r7s0's verified deferred-store/MUL diff (+2.1%). Remedies proposed and not tried (implementer's): drop the tag (one exact 16 KB window, hit = flop qualifier && valid as in r6s2) or register the meta output and take the hit one cycle late. Gotchas if reused: a 4096x9 array maps to two 2Kx9 BSRAMs plus an output mux on the hit path, so keep 4096x8 byte lanes (2 BSRAM each) and a separate 4096x4 `{valid, tag}` array (1 BSRAM) written on every completed op (value = allocate || clean hit) so the lane enables carry no hit term; a sub-word store may keep valid only on a clean first-cycle hit latched while it waits for the bus, otherwise it invalidates; a read whose index equals either write-pipeline stage is a forced miss; riscv-formal ties the dmem ready input, so 53/53 never exercises a shadow-served load and correctness rests on stalled cosim plus `test/test_dmem_shadow.py` (the regfile is not reset between cocotb runs, so compare stalled vs zero-stall runs from identical register state); `formal/run_all.sh` needs `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench` and `make cosim` needs `NRET=1`.

title: Load-value replay predictor: exact BSRAM shadow of the RAM window hides dmem stalls for loads (+ 1-entry store buffer)
motivation:
Every classic predictor lever is measured and spent on this champion: a perfect
direction predictor is worth <=2.4% (44k mispredicts, data-dependent, gshare no
better), a perfect RAS +0.80% (r5s2), steering-word/target replay +2.1% (r6s1).
All sit under the 4.6% bar. The one stall pool nobody has touched is the DATA
bus: ~192k of 3,682,766 CoreMark cycles (5.2%) are dmem-stall cycles (a
LOAD/STORE sitting in MEM while io_dmemReady=0, ~22% per cycle), and since r6s2
removed most fetch starvation a backend stall cycle now costs close to a full
cycle (r6s0 lesson: re-count, the old 22% discount is stale). r6s2 showed the
recipe that hides a 22% bus stall at ZERO Fmax cost: an untagged exact-address
BSRAM map read synchronously every cycle, with all hit qualifiers folded into
one flop so the only new term in the stall cone is `flop && bsram_valid_bit`.
This hypothesis is the data-side twin of that predictor. RAM is
0x00020000..0x0002FFFF (link.ld), written only by the core's own stores, so a
shadow that tracks every store is exact (no verify / no mis-speculation path).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(A) Load-value replay (the core of the slot). New module rtl/load_replay.sv,
instantiated from core.sv next to mem_stage:
  - Window: addr[31:16]==16'h0002 and addr[14:12]=={3{addr[15]}} -> two exact
    4 KB maps (bss/data at 0x20000.., stack at 0x2F000..), index =
    {addr[15], addr[11:2]} (11 bits). Implementer: confirm with an ISS trace
    that >90% of CoreMark loads fall in it; widen to 12 bits if not.
  - Storage: four byte-lane BSRAMs 2048x8 (syn_ramstyle="block_ram", plain
    SDPB, no byte enables needed) + one 2048x1 VALID BSRAM. Read is
    synchronous, bypass-mode, addressed by ex_stage's jalr_sum index bits
    (same adder that already feeds EX/MEM.mem_addr and the bench dmem BSRAM),
    read CE = !stall_ex_mem, so the word for the load arrives from the RAM
    output register in its MEM cycle. Use a dedicated syn_preserve'd address
    path if the first build loses Fmax through placement (r6s2 `pc_ra`).
  - Writes (one port, MEM stage, enable = !stall_ex_mem-type terms from
    io_dmemReady + EX/MEM flops only, no `fetch_acc`): a LOAD completing on
    the bus writes all four lanes with io_dmemRData and VALID=1; a STORE
    leaving MEM writes its wmask lanes with wdata_rep; VALID is written 1
    only by SW (full word) and is left untouched by SB/SH (a valid word
    stays valid and correct, an invalid one stays invalid). Misaligned ops
    never write.
  - Hit: every qualifier except the valid bit is computed in EX and folded
    into ONE flop captured with EX/MEM: rd_hit_q = load && in-window &&
    !(store in MEM at the capture edge: read-during-write hazard, flop-only
    test ex_mem.ctrl.mem_write) && !sweep_busy. Then
      dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && mem_op && !(rd_hit_q && valid_out)
    which is the SAME single LUT4 that computes dmem_stall today (no added
    level in stall_if/stall_id/stall_ex_mem/hold_mem_wb; only the launch
    point of that LUT gains a BSRAM clock-to-out). On a hit with the bus not
    ready the load completes this cycle from the shadow word:
    rdata_eff = dmem_ready ? io_dmemRData : shadow_word, feeding the existing
    load-extract and MEM/WB.mem_rdata (RVFI sees the true memory word).
    If the rdata_eff mux shows on the dmem -> load-extract -> MEM/WB path,
    duplicate the extract for the shadow word and merge in the last LUT.
  - Post-reset invalidation sweep of the VALID RAM on the write port (2048
    cycles, hits off while busy; BSRAM survives reset and cocotb reloads
    programs) - same scheme as if_stage's rs sweep; compiled out under
    RISCV_FORMAL (wrapper ties io_dmemReady=1, so the path is unreachable
    there and correctness rests on stalled cosim vs the ISS + a cocotb test).
  - Pipeline invariants untouched: stall_id/flush_id/stall_ex_mem/hold_mem_wb
    keep their meaning (a hit simply makes the cycle a non-stall cycle), so
    the registered forwarding selects stay valid.
Sizing: ~685k memory ops per run (192k stall cycles / 0.282), ~70% loads ->
~135k load-stall cycles; with ~85% window+valid hit rate ~110k cycles removed
= about +3% iter/cycle. Implementer must first count (cosim/ISS) loads, loads
directly behind a store, and window coverage, and replace the blanket
"store ahead => no hit" rule by an 11-bit index compare (jalr_sum idx ==
ex_mem.mem_addr idx -> one flop) only if that count says it matters.
(B) Stacked increment, only after (A) is validated and timing-neutral on an
--all-options median: a 1-entry store buffer in mem_stage. A STORE whose bus
cycle is not ready moves into {sb_addr, sb_wdata, sb_wen, sb_valid} and the
pipeline proceeds (the shadow is already updated when it leaves MEM); the
buffer owns io_dmemAddr/WData/WEn (flop-selected 2:1 on outputs) until
io_dmemReady. store_stall = sb_valid && !dmem_ready; load_stall = !hit &&
(sb_valid || !dmem_ready); a shadow-hit load never needs the bus. Removes
most of the remaining ~58k store-stall cycles (~+1.2%). MMIO stores
(addr[31:28]!=0) bypass the buffer so marker/UART timing is unchanged.
Fmax plan: no new adder, no new level in the stall network, no fetch-side
change; the only timing risks are BSRAM clock-to-out (~2.3 ns) at the head of
dmem_stall -> stall_if -> fetch_acc -> PC and placement pull of 5 more BSRAMs
on jalr_sum. Run `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` after (A);
if the median drops >2% fall back to gating only stall_ex_mem/stall_id with
the hit one build at a time, and drop (B) rather than ship a slower clock.
