lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-003-r7s2 (regression, -4.89%): Folding the load-shadow hit into one flop fixed the stall cone and still did not make a BSRAM that is read at the EX adder output free — scored 299.73 = 106.7 MHz median (evaluator's figure; 116.06 -> 106.7, -8.0%) x 3,560,666 CoreMark cycles (measured under `--istall --dstall`, CRCs valid; 122,100 of the ~192k dmem-stall cycles gone, +3.43% iter/cycle vs 3,682,766, 111% of the ~110k forecast; LUT4 2944 -> 2963, FF 849 -> 864, BSRAM 12 -> 17 of 46; formal 53/53 first try, stalled cosim clean; part (B), the 1-entry store buffer, not attempted) — and because it was built in the same round as r7s1 from the same idea it is the controlled half of that experiment: with r7s1's suspect (b) removed (untagged 2 x 4 KB exact window `addr[31:16]==2 && addr[14:12]=={3{addr[15]}}`, four 2048x8 lanes + a 2048x1 VALID RAM, every other qualifier in three EX/MEM-side flops so that `dmem_stall = !dmem_ready && (mem_nb_q || (ld_cand_q && !lr_valid))` is still one LUT4) the Fmax loss shrank from -18.3% to -8.0% and no path through `u_lr`, `ld_cand_q` or the stall network is in the top 5 of the one report that was printed (option 0, 103.5 MHz vs the champion's 107.6: ID/EX.pc, ID/EX.alu_op and MEM/WB.alu_result -> EX/MEM.alu_result plus EX/MEM.alu_result -> `upd_taken_q`, five paths tied inside 0.011 ns at 14.95 ns, i.e. the champion's own EX families ~0.36 ns slower), so what is left is r7s1's suspect (a) and it acts as placement/loading, not as a cone: the read address is still the combinational EX `jalr_sum` (`{[15],[11:2]}`, the end of forward mux -> rs1+imm adder) fanned out to 11 address pins on each of 5 more fixed-site BSRAMs, and unlike r6s2 the read also carries a clock enable from the stall network (`!stall_ex_mem`, needed to hold the word and VALID bit of a waiting load) — neither was isolated (scribe's reading, not a measurement), because this was once more a single build: `make timing` (option 0 only) started at lint-pass, no `--all-options`, no timing iteration, the options that set the median never printed, and the hypothesis's own fallback (a dedicated `syn_preserve`d address path, here a duplicated index adder) not tried. What follows: (1) "hit = flop && BSRAM valid bit" is necessary and not sufficient — r6s2 was free because its address pins were flops as well and even then needed four builds, whereas a table addressed from the EX adder has now cost -18% and -8% on its two first builds, so budget one as -8% until an `--all-options` median says otherwise; (2) the load shadow's prize is now measured rather than inferred and it is small — 2,048 words in 5 BSRAMs with the blanket "no hit when the op in MEM may write the shadow" rule (no index compare) recovered 122.1k cycles against ~127k inferred for r7s1's 4,096-word tagged 9-BSRAM version, so window coverage and the store-ahead hazard are not the limiter (the ~70k stall cycles left are, by the hypothesis's uncounted estimate, mostly the ~58k store stalls) and +3.43% is 326.0 at flat Fmax against the 329.7 bar (break-even with the champion at these cycles is 112.2 MHz, acceptance needs 117.4 MHz, above the champion's own 116.06): it cannot merge alone at any achievable Fmax, and stacked on r7s0's verified deferred-store/MUL diff (75,651 cycles) the pair gives ~3.485M cycles only if the two are additive (unverified; both rewrite `dmem_stall`), which clears the bar at >= 114.9 MHz — the stack has ~1% of Fmax to spend, so prove the shadow Fmax-neutral first or drop the data bus as a lever; (3) option 0 is the champion's low outlier (107.6/116.1/116.1) and in both shadow builds its delta understated the median's by 2-3x (-3.8% vs -8.0% here, -6.2% vs -18.3% in r7s1), so an option-0 `make timing` is not a proxy for the score and the first background job after lint should be `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`; (4) two of the three round-7 slots built the same load shadow in parallel and neither could read the other's lesson — de-duplicate hypotheses within a round. Gotchas if reused: the window test can stay off the 32-bit carry chain because `jalr_sum[31:12]` is `rs1[31:12]` -1/+0/+1, so three constant compares on `rs1[31:12]` are selected by `jalr_sum[12] ^ rs1[12]` and `imm[12]`; a load must fill the shadow only when it was a candidate and read VALID=0 (if every bus load fills, the write blocks the hit of the load behind it and a run of loads behind one store never hits); VALID is set only by SW or a load fill, SB/SH update their lanes and leave it alone, misaligned ops are never candidates and never write; pre-fold `mem_op && !ld_cand` into its own flop to keep the stall LUT at four inputs; the RAM is shrunk to 32 entries and the 2048-cycle post-reset VALID sweep compiled out under `RISCV_FORMAL`, where the dmem ready input is tied to 1, so 53/53 never exercises a shadow-served load — and here no cocotb test was written either (`test_load_replay.py` missing, the edited `test_pipeline.py`/`test_branch_pred.py` source lists not re-run), so correctness rested on stalled cosim vs the ISS alone.

title: Zero-Fmax bubble stack: typed replay entries (steer targets + not-taken branches) in the same 8 BSRAMs, on top of r7s0 deferred stores + MUL-as-load
motivation:
Fmax is walled at ~116 MHz by 4-5 tied datapath families (r5s0, r5s2, r6s0: removing
some of them moved the median by <= 0), so the only micro_opt lever left is
iterations/cycle, and every remaining item is 1-3% - below the 4.6% bar alone.
Champion: 3,682,766 cycles for ~2.92M instructions. Lost cycles: <=172k fetch-starved,
~192k dmem stalls, ~94k MUL bubbles, ~116k redirect slots, ~195k load-use.
Two things are known to be Fmax-neutral here and have never been combined:
(a) r7s0's verified, unmerged diff (deferred stores + MUL-as-load): 75,651 cycles,
    116.39 MHz median, formal 53/53, cosim clean - highest score ever measured (322.68),
    rejected only for being under the bar alone. Its lesson asks for "about as much
    again in the same build".
(b) r6s2's replay recipe (flop-addressed BSRAM, hit = one pre-folded flop AND one RAM
    bit, word enters only through the fetch FIFO) cost 0 Fmax. Today it covers only
    words reached SEQUENTIALLY that are never steering. Every word reached through a
    fetch-time steer (JAL fold / predicted-taken branch target) and every conditional
    branch word is still exposed to the 22% imem stall; r6s1 measured that residual at
    ~75k cycles but paid for it with tags, 3 extra BSRAMs, ~190 flops and a replayed
    immediate in front of the PC adder (-4.7% Fmax).
This slot gets most of that residual with NO new BSRAM, NO tag, NO adder/mux in the PC
loop, and stacks it on (a). Both halves touch disjoint files (if_stage.sv vs
ex/mem/hazard/muldiv), so they do not interact.

title: Bus-decoupled pipeline: write-behind store bus + MUL-in-MEM (r7s0 rebuild) stacked with a fetch-flow-indexed replay table
motivation:
Champion = 315.15 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 cycles for 2.92M instructions.
Fmax sits on a tied ~8.6 ns wall (ALU self-loop, compare, PHT loop, decode)
that r4s0/r5s0/r5s2/r6s0 could not move, so the lever left is iterations/cycle,
and no single item clears the 4.6% bar: r7s0 (deferred stores + MUL-as-load)
measured +2.10% (75,651 cycles) at NEUTRAL Fmax (116.39 MHz, reproduced 3x)
and lost only to the bar; its lesson says to rebuild it and stack an equally
sized item in the same build. Everything that touched an EX-adder-addressed
BSRAM (load shadow, r7s1/r7s2) cost 8-18% Fmax, so the stacked item must use
flop-driven RAM pins and a one-LUT hit, like r6s2. Remaining fetch starvation
(~172k cycles, scribe's split: ~100k steering words, ~54k non-steering words
at steer targets, ~16k redirect targets) offers exactly that: r6s2's table is
indexed "word at pc+4", so it can never serve the word after a folded JAL or
a predicted-taken branch, although that word is just as deterministic.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple BOTH memory buses from the pipeline registers, in one build, staged
so each part's cycles are counted separately (cosim --bench --istall --dstall
takes a minute; record cycles after A, after B, after C).

A (structural core, rebuild of verified r7s0, 75.6k cycles): dedicated bus
flops written in EX (mem_addr, bus_wdata, bus_wen, bus_ren, bus_act; byte
mask / replication / misalign gate computed in EX from jalr_sum[1:0]) with
their own enable !bus_hold; bus_busy = !dmem_ready && bus_act;
dmem_stall = bus_busy && (bus_ren || (id_ex.bus_sync && !redirect)) with
bus_sync = mem_read | mem_write | opcode==SYSTEM pre-decoded into one ID/EX
flop. A not-ready STORE retires while its write waits in the bus flops; no
store buffer, no address compare, io_dmemAddr stays a pure flop (the bench
dmem BSRAM must keep absorbing it). MUL becomes load-like: operands captured
every !stall cycle, DSP product ORed in front of MEM/WB.alu_result, no
ex_busy for MUL, load-use detector widened to mem_read | is_mul (do NOT
pre-OR that into an extra flop: measured 108 MHz). DIV unchanged.

B (new, ~54k cycles est., no new cone): re-index the replay BSRAM by the
PREDECESSOR in fetch order instead of by address-4. Entry i (same 4096 depth,
32 bits = same 8 BSRAM) = {valid, dir, instr[31:2]} of the word that was
fetched right after the word at 4*i, where dir = that predecessor's steer_eff
(0 = fell through, 1 = folded JAL / predicted-taken branch target). Read
stays as is (pc_ra flops, every cycle, no CE): rs_out at t+1 is the successor
of pc(t). hit_q <= fetch_acc && ok_d loses its !steer_eff term (and the
rs_idx != '1 term); a new flop dir_q <= steer_eff; rs_hit = hit_q &&
rs_out.valid && (rs_out.dir == dir_q), still ONE LUT4 behind the RAM. Only
non-steering successors are stored, so a hit still means pc <= pc+4 and the
PC mux, the adder and the PHT loop are untouched. Write (registered,
idempotent, no stall term): prev_idx_q <= rs_idx every cycle (no CE),
prev_acc_q <= fetch_acc && rs_win; w_en_q <= swp_busy || (imem_ready &&
prev_acc_q && rs_store); w_idx_q <= prev_idx_q (the rs_idx-1 decrementer
goes away); w_data_q <= {!swp_busy, dir_q, imem_data[31:2]}. The stored word
is exact because next(P) is a pure function of (word at P, dir) and code in
the window is stable (rs_off / rs_kill / post-reset sweep kept as is).

C (optional, ~37k est.; keep only if the median holds): also store aligned
legal conditional branches as successors with one more bit is_br, and replay
them only when the PHT read at the current pc says not-taken
(rs_hit &&= !rs_out.is_br || !pht_rd[1]; pred_taken = 0, pred_ctr = pht_rd,
pc <= pc+4). Needs no stored target and no adder behind the RAM.

Arithmetic: A+B = ~130k -> 3.553M cycles (+3.6%); A+B+C = ~167k -> 3.516M
(+4.7%) at flat Fmax, so the stack has no Fmax to spend: start
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` right after lint, judge by
the median (never option 0), and drop C if it costs anything. Formal ties
both ready inputs, so correctness of A/B rests on stalled cosim vs the ISS
plus the cocotb tests below.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-002-r8s1 (regression, -3.43%): Two bubble removals that were each Fmax-neutral when built alone did not stay neutral when stacked, and the Fmax given back was larger than the whole stack's cycle prize — scored 304.33 vs the champion's 315.15, and since fitness = Fmax[MHz] x 1e7 / cycles (checks on r6s2 and r7s0) the median must have fallen to ~108 MHz if cycles reached the A+B forecast of ~3.553M, 109.8 MHz if only A's measured 3,607,115 was reached, and could not be above 112.1 MHz even with no cycle gain at all (scribe's inference: no Fmax, cycle count, per-stage A/B count, timing report or implementer notes reached the scribe; the submitted RTL is A + B without C — `rs_store` still excludes `br_ok`, no `is_br` bit, `rs_hit = hit_q && rs_out[31] && (rs_out[30] == dir_q)`, `prev_idx_q`/`prev_acc_q`/`dir_q` write side as specified) — i.e. a 5-7% Fmax loss against a +3.6% iter/cycle forecast, with no new cone to blame: the replay BSRAM is still read from the `pc_ra` flops with no CE, the hit is still one LUT behind the RAM, and the PC mux, adder and PHT loop are untouched. Sibling r8s0 (same round, scribe timed out, so recorded here) is the same experiment with different names — r7s0's A plus a source-keyed `{valid_tgt, valid_seq, instr[31:2]}` table (`src_idx_q`/`src_tgt_q`/`src_ok_q`, `rs_hit = (rs_out[31] && thit_q) || (rs_out[30] && hit_q)`, not-taken-predicted branches stored too) — and measured 3,537,575 cycles (145,191 saved, +4.10% iter/cycle, formal + cosim clean) at a 112.02 MHz median (107.8/112.0/112.0; LUT4 2879, FF 873, 12 BSRAM) = 316.65, +0.48%: so the predecessor-indexed replay table works and is worth ~70k cycles on top of A's 75.6k, but A-alone (116.39), the plain table (116.06) and A + re-keyed table (112.0 and ~108) show that 'zero Fmax when measured alone' is a statement about one placement, not an additive property — with 4-5 families tied inside ~0.1 ns at the 8.6 ns wall, every netlist change re-rolls which family loses, medians of near-identical variants of this core have ranged 104-116 MHz (r6s2's four builds: 108.9/103.9/107.8/116.06), and the champion's 116.06 is the best of those draws, so a first build of any stacked diff should be budgeted at ~4-7% below the champion's Fmax, not at parity (unattributed candidates specific to this diff, none measured: the second RAM bit `dir` in `rs_hit` -> `fetch_acc`, `hit_q` now armed after steered accepts so replay words enter the FIFO on the cycle after a PHT-steered pc update, and three files' worth of EX/MEM bus flops re-placed next to the dmem BSRAM). Rules: (1) the fetch+backend bubble stack is now measured at its ceiling — r8s0's 3,537,575 cycles would score 328.1 at 116.06 MHz and 329.0 at 116.39, still under the 329.7 bar even with ALL the Fmax recovered — so a third rebuild of 'A + replay coverage' cannot merge by itself; it needs another >= 20-40k cycles from an untouched pool (load-use ~195k, redirect slots ~116k) AND a held median, or a lower bar; (2) a stacked hypothesis must spend its slot on timing iterations, not on more features: start from the verified r8s0 diff, run `--all-options` after each part (A, then B) and print the top-5 of the two median options so the part that moves the median is identified — r7s1 and r7s2 ended with a single unprinted build and r8s1 left no timing record at all, so three slots in a row carry an unattributed Fmax loss; (3) report cycles and the three option Fmax values in the implementation notes — a result with neither can only be bracketed, as above.

title: Path-predicted next-fetch replay: BSRAM successor predictor also covers branches, JALs and steer targets
motivation:
The r6s2 champion (315.15 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 cycles) hides imem stalls only
for NON-steering words reached SEQUENTIALLY. Every branch / JAL word and every word
reached through a fetch-time steer (folded JAL, predicted-taken branch) is still
exposed to the 22% imem stall. Direction and return prediction are spent (ceilings
2.2% / 0.8%), so the remaining predictor prize is predicting the NEXT FETCHED WORD on
the predicted path. MEASURED at hypothesis time (RTL prototype in if_stage.sv only,
stalled cosim --istall --dstall, CRCs valid, "none" config reproduces 3,682,766):
  T1 replay not-taken-predicted branch words (hit gated by live PHT)  3,657,443 +0.69%
  T2 steer-target words (predecessor-indexed entry + path bit)        3,648,657 +0.93%
  T1+T2                                                               3,623,333 +1.64%
  T1+T2+T3 (T3 = also replay taken branches / folded JALs)            3,594,417 +2.46%
Negative result: "store a branch iff it did not steer when last fetched live" with
no PHT at replay time is WORSE than the champion (3,719,678, -1.0%): stale
not-taken replays of loop branches mispredict. The replay must use the live PHT.
Honest sizing: +2.46% iter/cycle is under the 4.6% bar alone, Fmax is NOT measured
(no time for a Gowin run). The change is confined to if_stage.sv so it stacks with
the verified, unmerged r7s0 backend diff (+2.10%, Fmax-neutral); if additive the
pair is ~3,519k cycles = +4.7%.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
PART A (the hypothesis; if_stage.sv only). Generalise rs_mem from "word at pc+4" to
"successor word on the predicted path", keeping r6s2's Fmax-free recipe: same
4096-entry untagged BSRAM, same flop-driven read address pc_ra, no clock enable,
replayed word only into the FIFO data flops, registered write without stall/fetch_acc.
- Entry = {valid, path, jal_r, br_r, instr[31:2]} (34 bits, 4-bit lanes, 9 BSRAM).
  jal_r/br_r are the stored jal_fold/br_ok pre-decode of the successor word; all
  words with low bits 11 are stored.
- Predecessor flops ppc_q[11:0], pvalid_q, pst_q (loaded on fetch_acc with rs_idx,
  rs_win, steer_eff; pvalid_q cleared on reset/redirect). Write index =
  (pvalid_q && pst_q) ? ppc_q : rs_idx-1, path bit = pvalid_q && pst_q, enable =
  imem_ready && rs_win && rs_store && (path || rs_idx != 0): all flops + imem_ready.
- Two pre-folded flops replace hit_q: hit_seq_q <= fetch_acc && !steer_eff && ok_d &&
  rs_idx != '1, hit_str_q <= fetch_acc && steer_eff && ok_d.
  rs_hit = valid && (path ? hit_str_q : hit_seq_q): still ONE LUT4 behind the BSRAM

title: Zero-bubble load->branch: resolve load-dependent branches in MEM (late compare), stacked on r7s0's deferred-store bus + MUL-as-load
motivation:
Champion r6s2 = 315.15 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 cycles; the bar is 329.7.
Fmax is a 4-5 family tie that ten slots of reshaping have not moved, and the
fetch-side pool is closed (r8s0/r8s1/r8s2: 13 builds, none back at 116).
The only large pool nobody has touched is the load-use bubble (~195k
bubbles, r5s0 count). MEASURED at hypothesis time (ISS trace of
bench/programs/coremark.elf between the markers, 2,922,016 instructions,
544,852 loads): 204,039 load-use pairs, and the consumer is a conditional
BRANCH in 135,320 of them (66%); LOAD base 59,350, OP-IMM 7,949, OP 1,000,
STORE 420. (MUL-use: 35,640 = OP 32,400 + STORE 3,240, no branches.)
So two thirds of all load-use bubbles are load -> branch (core_state byte
scan, list find/traverse: lbu/lh/lw then beq/bne).
A branch does not need its operand in EX at all: it was already predicted
at fetch, EX only VERIFIES it. Verifying one stage later costs nothing when
the prediction was right (bubble removed) and exactly the same 3 slots when
it was wrong (today: 1 bubble + 2 redirect slots; late: 3 redirect slots),
so cycles can only go down. r7s0's verified, Fmax-neutral backend diff
(deferred stores + MUL-as-load, 3,607,115 cycles, 116.39 MHz, 322.68) was
2.4% short alone; this adds the missing untouched-pool increment in the
same backend files.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
PART 1 (new) - late branch resolve for load-dependent branches.
ID: when the load-use detector matches AND the ID word is a legal
conditional branch with an aligned target (br_ok; fetch already pre-decodes
it - bank one `is_br` bit per FIFO entry and export it in if_id_t so the
hazard LUT gets a ready bit, and pre-fold `id_ex.mem_read && rd != 0` into
one ID/EX flop so the final hazard LUT stays 4-input:
load_use = ld_q && (eq1 || eq2) && !is_br), do NOT stall: the branch enters
ID/EX with late_rs1/late_rs2 flags (which operand matched the load's rd) and
`late` = their OR. br_bad branches keep the bubble (trap depends on cond).
EX: a `late` branch does not mispredict, does not train the PHT; it is
captured in EX/MEM with late flags, pred_taken, pred_ctr, branch_op, and
its mp_target (pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm) in a new late_target flop.
MEM (the load is now in WB, MEM/WB.alu_result is its data, a plain flop):
second comparator a = late_rs1 ? mem_wb.alu_result : ex_mem.rs1_val (same
for b), one == and one unsigned < with the same cmp_flip fold as EX.
late_miss = late && (cond != pred_taken). It feeds only flops:
redir_q <= (mispredict && !stall) || late_miss (same single redirect flop
drives PC / v0,v1 / flush_id exactly as today), redir_late_q <= late_miss
(selects late_target_q over redir_target_q, flop-launched 2:1), and the
registered PHT training flops (upd_* take the MEM branch when late).
A branch in MEM is never a memory op, so no dmem stall can hold that cycle.
Squash on a late redirect: the wrong-path instruction in EX is squashed by
the existing redir_q mechanism; the one that already reached MEM is killed
by redir_late_q (flop): gate dmem_wen/dmem_ren (or r7s0 bus_wen/bus_ren),
the mem-op term of dmem_stall, mem_w_en, rs_kill, and MEM/WB valid/ctrl
capture. Add an abort (redir_late_q) to muldiv so a wrong-path DIV started
one cycle earlier returns to IDLE. redir_late_q wins over a wrong-path
redirect raised in the same cycle. RVFI (untimed): MEM/WB gets the fixed-up
rs1/rs2 values and pc_next = late cond ? branch_target : pc+4.
Forwarding invariant (r2s0) is untouched: no new stall/hold, ID/EX still
captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB advance; the stale select-01 value
for the load operand is simply replaced in MEM.
PART 2 - re-apply r7s0 as logged (measured 75,651 cycles, Fmax-neutral):
dedicated EX/MEM bus flops (mem_addr, bus_wdata, bus_wen, bus_ren, bus_act)
with enable !bus_hold so a not-ready STORE does not freeze the pipeline
(dmem_stall = bus_busy && (bus_ren || (id_ex.bus_sync && !redirect)),
bus_sync = mem_read | mem_write | SYSTEM), and MUL-as-load (operands
captured every !stall cycle, product ORed in front of MEM/WB.alu_result,
load-use widened to mem_read | is_mul; a late branch behind a MUL uses the
same MEM-stage compare since the product is in MEM/WB.alu_result one cycle
later exactly like load data).
Method (mandatory): first add a cosim counter on the champion for
load-use bubbles whose ID word is a br_ok branch and for the fraction
predicted correctly - that count IS the Part 1 prize; build Part 2 first
(known-good), then Part 1; after each part record CoreMark cycles and run
`python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`, printing the top-5 paths
of the median options. If the MEM comparator or the hazard `!is_br` term
shows up on top, fall back to registering the compare operands (compare in
WB, 4-slot late penalty) before dropping the part. Sizing: 135,320
load->branch bubbles; a mispredicted one costs the same as today, so the
prize is the correctly predicted share (all branches: 44.3k mispredicts,
so >= ~100-120k bubbles removed). At r7s0's measured ~0.75 cycles per
backend bubble that is ~80-100k cycles (+2.2..2.8%) for Part 1 alone and
~155-175k (3.51-3.53M cycles, +4.4..5.0%) with Part 2's measured 75.6k;
329.7 needs <= 3,520k at 116.06 MHz. Part 1 is the larger, new half - if
time runs short ship Part 1 + MUL-as-load-free Part 2 store deferral only
after Part 1 is timed; never ship a half-wired late path (formal exercises
it fully: load->branch needs no bus stall, so riscv-formal covers Part 1).

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-001-r9s0 (regression, -3.50%): Resolving load-dependent branches one stage late (no load-use bubble for a load -> branch pair, compare in MEM against MEM/WB.alu_result) delivered more cycles than forecast and still lost, because the exemption itself sits on the core's tied-critical stall cone — 304.13 = 108.33 MHz median (93.2/108.3/108.3; the champion RTL rebuilt in the same session reproduced 116.064 = 107.6/116.06/116.06, so the loss is the change and not run-to-run noise) x 3,561,985 CoreMark cycles (measured under `--istall --dstall`, CRCs valid; 120,781 saved, +3.39% iter/cycle vs 3,682,766; LUT4 2944 -> 3085, FF 849 -> 970; formal 53/53 first try, cosim clean; Part 1 only — the r7s0 stack was not built). What it established: (a) the load-use pool is mostly branches and they are well predicted — the hypothesis's ISS trace counted 204,039 load-use pairs with a conditional branch as the consumer in 135,320 (66%; LOAD base 59,350, OP-IMM 7,949, OP 1,000, STORE 420), and exempting them saved 0.89 cycles per pair against the 0.75 assumed (the 80-100k forecast was 20-50% low), a prize the size of r7s2's load shadow (122.1k); (b) it is not free: `load_use = ld && (eq1 || eq2) && !is_br` makes the stall depend on the instruction CLASS of the ID word, and for the live (FIFO-bypass) word `is_br` is a pre-decode behind `imem_ready`, so the term lands on the lfsr -> `imem_ready` -> hazard -> `stall` -> `fetch_acc` -> PC/`hit_q` family that already tops the champion's reports — first build 105.3 MHz with one extra LUT level (~0.86 ns) there because synthesis shared `ld && (eq1 || eq2)` between the stall and the late-detect; splitting them with kept nets (`lu_en`/`other_stall`) moved the top to MEM/WB.alu_result -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result at 102.4 (the forwarding net had picked up the second comparator's 64 loads); preserved private copies `late_wb_q`/`late_wr_q` gave the shipped 108.33 with five paths inside 6 ps at 14.52 ns, `imem_ready` -> `br_ok_eff` (3 LUTs) -> `lu_en` -> `stall` -> `hit_q` among them; dropping `imem_ready` from `is_br` cleared that path and scored 104.6 with `pc` -> `late_target_q`/`redir_target_q` and `late_rs2` -> `redir_q` (the MEM comparator, 10 cells) on top, and three more variants came back at 97.0-103.0 — seven builds, none at the 112.3 MHz break-even, i.e. +141 LUT / +121 FF placed in the EX/MEM + fetch-stall region that already held the 4-5 family tie cost ~7% whichever cone was trimmed (implementer's reading: every family within ~0.3 ns, +-4 MHz per perturbation); (c) the arithmetic was against the shipped half from the start: 3,561,985 cycles at the champion's 116.06 MHz is 325.8, under the 329.7 bar (acceptance alone needs 117.4 MHz), and with r7s0's 75,651 cycles (additivity unverified) the pair is ~3.486M, which clears the bar only at >= 114.9 MHz against the 108.3 measured — so the stack never had the Fmax to spend, and it is not a paste job either: deferred stores break the invariant "a branch in MEM is never held" that the late kill relies on (needs a hold-aware late compare; implementer's reading, untested), which is why a two-part hypothesis whose new half alone took seven timing builds did not fit a 30-minute slot. What follows (scribe's reading): a second, late resolution point is worth its ~120k cycles only if the bubble decision stays flop-only for BOTH FIFO and live words and no second 32-bit target/comparator lands on the EX/MEM flops — untried: bank the exemption bit per FIFO entry and keep the bubble for the live-bypass word, recompute the late target from EX/MEM.pc instead of `late_target_q` + a 2:1 in front of PC, or compare in WB from registered operands (4 slots on a late mispredict); budget any of them at -7% Fmax until an `--all-options` median says otherwise, and give any second reader of MEM/WB.alu_result its own preserved flops from the first build. Gotchas if reused: a misaligned (trapping) LOAD in front of the late branch writes no rd, so the MEM operand select needs MEM/WB.reg_write and the branch's EX forward select for that operand must be the pre-load value, never 01 (EX/MEM.alu_result is the load's address there; `forward_unit.ex_kill`); `redir_late_q` must gate dmem wen/ren, MEM/WB.valid, `rs_kill` and the dmem-stall term and abort muldiv (a wrong-path DIV started one cycle earlier), while `mem_w_en` needs no gate (`flush_id` is 1 on the kill cycle); a late branch in MEM and a normal branch in EX can resolve in the same cycle and share one PHT training slot (late wins, the EX one is wrong-path if the late one missed).

title: Late branch resolve in MEM: load-dependent branches skip the load-use bubble (+ MUL as load-like op)
motivation:
Champion r6s2 = 116.06 MHz x 3,682,766 CoreMark cycles (2,922,015 insns).
Fmax is walled by 4-5 tied datapath families and every fetch-side or
data-bus add-on since has cost more Fmax than its cycles, so the remaining
lever is a backend bubble pool that needs NO new table, BSRAM or fetch
logic. The largest untouched pool is load-use (~200k bubbles). I traced it
with the Python ISS (test/cosim/reference.py on coremark.elf, between the
markers, bimodal PHT modelled - it reproduces the measured mispredict
count 44,266 vs 44,289):
  load-use pairs (DUT's field-based detector)   204,039
    consumer is a conditional BRANCH            135,320  (66%)
    consumer is a LOAD (address, unfixable)      59,350
    consumer is a STORE                           3,560
    consumer is any ALU op                        ~9,000  (a "late ALU" is worthless)
  of the 135,320 load->branch pairs only 2,092 (1.5%) are mispredicted,
  and in 124,989 the branch is predicted correctly AND the next
  instruction is not a branch / JALR / M op.
So 124,989 bubbles (3.4% of all cycles) exist only because a correctly
predicted branch waits in ID for load data it does not need until its
compare. Resolving exactly those branches one stage later (in MEM, where
the load data sits in the MEM/WB.alu_result flop) deletes the bubble; a
mispredicted one costs 0 + 3 slots instead of 1 + 2, i.e. nothing.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
PART A (mandatory, time it first with `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench
--all-options` and print the top-5 of the two median options).
Late branch = aligned legal conditional branch in ID (if_stage's `br_ok`
pre-decode; misaligned-target branches keep today's bubble and EX trap)
whose rs1/rs2 matches the rd of a LOAD in EX.
1. hazard: do not raise load_use_hazard for such a branch. Carry a 1-bit
   `is_brok` with the fetch word (FIFO flops bk0/bk1 next to pt0/ct0; live
   leg = existing br_ok && imem_ready) so the qualifier is one extra input
   of the LUT that already combines the two 5-bit matches (r6s0 lost Fmax
   by decoding instr bits behind the instr mux - do NOT do that).
2. ID/EX: new flops late_a / late_b (per operand: matched the load in EX)
   and late_br = late_a|late_b; for a late branch force br_ok=0, br_bad=0,
   pred bits kept, so EX neither redirects nor trains for it.
3. EX/MEM: carry late_a, late_b, late_pend (= valid late branch),
   pred_taken, pred_ctr; rs1_val / write_data (the forwarded rs1/rs2, now
   timed flops) are the non-late operands. `redir_target_q` already
   captured this branch's alternative target (mp_target) while it was in
   EX: just give it CE = !out.late_pend so it is held one more cycle - no
   new target flops, no mux in front of PC.
4. MEM: a = late_a ? MEM/WB.alu_result : rs1_val, b likewise, one == and
   one unsigned < exactly as in ex_stage (cmp_flip, pred_taken folded in);
   late_mis = late_pend && (cond != pred_taken). All inputs are flops and
   the mux is 2:1 flop-selected, so this cone is shorter than the EX
   compare family. redir_q <= (mispredict && !stall) || late_mis; the
   redirect flop then drives PC / v0,v1 / flush_id exactly as today (r4s1).
5. Squash: on late_mis the instruction in EX (B+1) must not reach MEM:
   clear only {valid, mem_read, mem_write, reg_write} of EX/MEM at capture
   (4 flops; fallback: kill it in MEM from a flop). B+2 is squashed by the
   existing redir_q rule, B+3 by flush_id. To keep ONE redirect register
   and never squash a started M op, a branch / JALR / M op in ID directly
   behind a late branch in EX takes the bubble instead (stall term =
   ID/EX.late_br flop && 1-bit `is_ctl` pre-decode carried with the fetch
   word like is_brok; superset decodes are fine; 8,239 cases, no loss vs
   today). Hence when late_pend, EX never redirects, trains or starts M.
6. PHT training: upd_en_q/upd_taken_q/upd_idx_q/upd_ctr_q take the MEM
   values when late_pend (flop-selected). RVFI: MEM/WB.pc_next, rs1_val,
   rs2_val are patched in MEM for a late branch (untimed).
The registered forwarding selects stay valid: load and branch still
advance in lockstep (a branch in MEM is never a memory op, so MEM/WB holds
the load data exactly in the branch's MEM cycle; a dmem stall of the load
freezes both). riscv-formal exercises all of this (no bus-stall needed).
PART B (mandatory, second): MUL as a load-like op exactly as verified in
r6s0/r7s0 (operand flops captured with !stall, product ORed in front of
MEM/WB.alu_result, no ex_busy for MUL, late-producer = mem_read | is_mul so
a MUL->branch is late too): ~94k MUL bubbles out, 34.5k MUL-use in.
Sizing: A removes 125k raw bubbles, B ~60k net; at r7s0's measured 0.75
cycles per raw bubble that is ~139k cycles (3.54M, +3.9%), at 0.9 ~166k
(+4.7%). STRETCH only if A+B time at >= 115 MHz median: r7s0's deferred
store bus flops (~35k cycles). Timing fallback if the median drops: resolve
ALL conditional branches in MEM and delete the EX comparator (one tied
family and ~100 LUT gone, costs 44k extra mispredict slots).

title: Predict through load-use: a branch fed by a load skips the bubble and is resolved one stage late (MEM) against the PHT prediction
motivation:
Direction/target prediction itself is spent on this champion (perfect
direction <= 2.4%, RAS measured +0.8%, gshare == bimodal), but the
existing bimodal prediction can still buy a pool nobody has touched:
the load-use bubble. Counted at hypothesis time with the Python ISS on
the scored CoreMark window (2,922,015 instrs - matches r5s0's count;
44,271 bimodal mispredicts vs 44,289 measured in RTL):
  load-use pairs (hazard_unit's own rs1/rs2 field compare): 204,039
    consumer = conditional BRANCH : 135,320  (66%)
    consumer = LOAD (pointer chase):  59,350
    consumer = OP-IMM/OP/STORE     :   9,369
  of the 135,320 load->branch pairs the 256x2b PHT at pc[9:2] predicts
  133,229 correctly (98.5% - list walks, null checks, loop exits).
Today every one of those branches waits a bubble for the load data only
to confirm a prediction fetch has already acted on. Nothing downstream
needs a branch's compare result, so the bubble is pure waste whenever
the prediction is right: 133k bubbles = 3.6% of the 3,682,766 cycles,
the largest single remaining pool and bigger than all remaining
branch-mispredict slots together.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
A conditional branch in ID whose rs1/rs2 matches the LOAD in EX is no
longer bubbled. It enters EX flagged defer_rs1/defer_rs2, does NOT
resolve there, and is resolved one cycle later in MEM, where the load
sits in MEM/WB (plain flops):
  opA = defer_rs1 ? MEM/WB.alu_result : EX/MEM.rs1_val   (same for B)
  late_miss = EX/MEM.late_br && (cond(opA,opB,branch_op) ^ pred_taken)
Right prediction (98.5%): the bubble is gone, 1 cycle saved. Wrong:
3 squashed slots instead of bubble + 2 slots - identical cost to today.
So it cannot lose cycles; forecast 100-133k cycles saved (r7s0 measured
~75% of raw backend bubbles as real cycles) = +2.8..3.7% iter/cycle.
Formal DOES exercise this path (no bus stall needed), unlike the replay
tables.

Mechanics - every existing invariant kept (stall_id / flush_id /
stall_ex_mem / hold_mem_wb equations unchanged apart from the hazard
qualifier, so ID/EX still captures exactly when EX/MEM and MEM/WB
advance and the registered forwarding selects stay valid):
1. hazard_unit: load_use_hazard &= !id_is_br, id_is_br =
   if_id.instr[6:2] == 5'b11000 (5 bits, parallel to the rd compares).
   Export the two per-operand matches (mem_read && rd!=0 && rd==rs1 /
   rs2) AND id_is_br as defer_rs1/defer_rs2 into ID/EX. Everything
   downstream keys on these flags, not on legality.
2. EX, instruction flagged defer: excluded from `mispredict` and from
   EX PHT training. EX/MEM gains real (timed) flops: late_br (= valid
   && defer && br_ok), defer_rs1/2, pred_taken, pred_ctr, and uses the
   existing rs1_val/rs2_val/pc/branch_op. All are zeroed by the
   existing bubble arm (ex_busy || redir_q).
3. Late redirect reuses the SAME flops - no mux in front of PC / FIFO
   valids / flush_id (r4s1 rule):
     redir_q <= late_miss || (mispredict && !stall && !late_miss)
     redir_target_q: clock-enable = !late_miss. It already holds the
     deferred branch's alternate target (loaded with mp_target on the
     edge the branch left EX; a branch is never held in MEM).
   The instruction in EX during the late-resolve cycle is wrong-path on
   late_miss: EX/MEM bubble arm becomes ex_busy || redir_q || late_miss,
   so the redirect cycle still has a non-memory bubble in MEM (the
   "redirect cycle is never dmem-held" property survives). The next one
   is squashed by redir_q exactly as today. A wrong-path M op that
   started in that cycle is cancelled by a flop-driven muldiv abort
   (abort = redir_q -> S_IDLE, both ALTOPS and real FSM).
4. Load that traps (misaligned, known from EX/MEM flops while the
   deferred instruction is in EX): its rd is not written, so the
   deferred operand does not exist in MEM/WB. Re-fetch: treat as a
   redirect to the deferred instruction's own pc and squash it
   (refetch = in.defer && ex_mem load-misalign; folded into the
   non-JALR arm of mp_target so the jalr_sum path gets no extra level).
5. PHT training of a late branch: second registered update set
   (lupd_*) from the MEM compare, sharing the one write port (late
   wins a same-cycle collision - hint-only loss).
6. RVFI-only (pruned from timing): MEM/WB.rs?_val <= defer ? MEM/WB
   .alu_result : EX/MEM.rs?_val for ANY flagged instruction (also
   reserved funct3 2/3, cosim/formal compare rs?_rdata regardless);
   pc_next and the br_bad taken->trap bit from the late outcome
   (br_bad never redirects, so late_br requires br_ok).

Timing plan (Fmax is the whole risk; 116.06 is the top of this
design's placement distribution, budget -3..-5% on a first build):
start `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options` as soon as
lint + selftest cosim pass and print the top-5 of the median options.
Known pressure points and their pre-planned remedies:
 (a) r6s0 saw -3.9% (one sample) from qualifying the load-use compare
     with instr bits (imem word -> hazard -> stall -> fetch_acc -> PC).
     If that cone leads: take the bit from if_stage instead (a `br`
     flop per FIFO entry for v0, the existing br-opcode pre-decode of
     imem_data for the bypass) so only one late 2:1 joins the compare.
 (b) late_miss (flop -> 2:1 -> 32-bit compare -> 1 LUT) fans out to
     redir_q D, the redir_target_q CE and the EX/MEM ctrl/valid bubble
     arm. It has no 3:1 forward mux in front, so it should sit under
     the EX compare family; if it leads, register the bubble instead
     (late_kill_q gating dmem_wen/ren, dmem_stall's mem_op term and
     MEM/WB valid/ctrl in the redirect cycle - all single-flop terms).
 (c) do not touch the EX result mux, PC mux, PHT read or replay table.
Report cycles (cosim --bench --istall --dstall) and all three option
Fmax values in the notes. Honest sizing: +3% at flat Fmax is below the
4.6% bar by itself; it merges only if the median holds or rises, but
it is the largest cycle pool left that costs no fetch-side state, and
the verified diff (135k-pair pool) is the natural base for a stack.

lesson: - 2026-11-25 hyp-20261125-003-r9s2 (regression, -9.06%): The third independent build of the same late-resolve idea in one round (siblings r9s0 and r9s1) reproduced the cycle prize to the cycle and landed lowest on Fmax, which closes the idea rather than any one implementation of it — 286.61 = 102.09 MHz median x 3,561,985 CoreMark cycles (measured under `--istall --dstall`, CRCs valid, identical to r9s0's count; +3.39% iter/cycle vs 3,682,766; LUT4 2944 -> 3070; formal 53/53, cosim clean) against r9s0's 108.33 and r9s1's 110.5 MHz (309.53), so three samples span 102-110.5 MHz and none reaches the ~112.3 MHz break-even, let alone the 117.4 MHz the 4.6% bar needs at this cycle count; this variant was the "cheap" one — no second target register and no mux in front of PC (`redir_q <= late_miss || ...`, `redir_target_q` clock-enabled by `!late_miss`), operand B taken from the already-timed EX/MEM.write_data, late PHT training sharing the existing update flops, `is_br` straight from `if_id.instr[6:2]` in hazard_unit — and it still came back -12% with the champion's tie intact but shifted ~1.2 ns: muldiv `rem_q` -> EX/MEM.alu_result, `fwd_a` -> EX/MEM.alu_result, EX/MEM.alu_result -> `redir_q` (10 cells) and `imem_ready` -> hazard -> ID -> `v0` (9 cells) all within ~5 ps of each other, i.e. there was no single new cone to trim, the cost is the instruction-class qualifier on the load-use stall plus a second 32-bit comparator and its ~60 flops packed into the EX/MEM region, which r9s0's "share the redirect flops" remedy does not touch. Rules that follow (scribe's reading): a +3.4% cycle prize cannot merge on a design whose Fmax sits at the top of its placement distribution unless the change adds essentially no logic near EX/MEM or the fetch-stall cone (any ~125-LUT addition there has cost 5-12% in every sample since r7s1), so the load->branch pool should be treated as spent until Fmax headroom exists; and when the round's slots converge on one mechanism the round buys one data point at three slots' cost — the cycle half was already known from the ISS count (135,320 pairs x ~0.89), so sibling slots should differ in the Fmax-relevant structure (e.g. per-FIFO-entry `br` bit with the bubble kept for the live-bypass word, or compare in WB from registered operands) or attack a different pool, not re-derive the same number.
